title.rendered: 15 Valentine’s Day iPhone Wallpapers in 4K (Free Download)

content.rendered:
Valentine’s Day is the perfect excuse to give your iPhone a little love makeover. Whether you’re into soft romance, bold hearts, or adorable vibes, a good wallpaper can instantly set the mood every time you unlock your phone.

Here are some of the sweetest 4K Valentine’s Day wallpapers you’ll want on your iPhone screen. Explore the collection and download your favorite one for free!

Table of Contents
  • 1. Cute Panda with Heart Balloon
  • 2. Minimal Split Heart Background
  • 3. Cozy Heart Valentine Wallpaper
  • 4. Floating Hearts on Dark Background
  • 5. Love Heart Minimal Art
  • 6. Rose Day iPhone Wallpaper
  • 7. A Couple Sitting Under a Starry Sky
  • 8. Couples Kissing Wallpaper
  • 9. Snoopy Valentine's Day
  • 10. Anime Heartwarming
  • 11. Wired Heart
  • 12. Butterfly Heart
  • 13. Wild hearts wallpaper
  • 14. Layered love Valentine's week
  • 15. Valentine's Day teddy
  • Celebrate Valentine's Day in Style!

1. Cute Panda with Heart Balloon 

This cute panda with a red heart balloon wallpaper is all about cuteness overload. The soft lighting and solid background keep it minimal and sweet, not dramatic.



Download

2. Minimal Split Heart Background 

A simple heart split across two shades of pink gives your screen a modern, subtle Valentine look. It is minimal enough for your app icons to be visible, yet aesthetic and romantic.

Download

3. Cozy Heart Valentine Wallpaper 

Three soft hearts resting on a warm pink background feel like a gentle hug for your screen. The textured backdrop adds depth, making it look artistic without being busy.

Download

4. Floating Hearts on Dark Background 

Looking for black wallpaper to match the iPhone’s dark theme? Here’s one with red hearts popping against a dark background, creating a stunning contrast. It is romantic and modern at the same time.

Download

5. Love Heart Minimal Art 

A red heart balloon floating above the word “Love” keeps things clean and emotional. The design adds just the right romantic touch to make your Lock Screen stand out.

Download

6. Rose Day iPhone Wallpaper

It’s common to delight partners with a rose. However, if you can’t give them roses on a Valentine’s Day movie date, offer them this free iPhone Valentine’s Day wallpaper. You’ll surely make an impression!

Download

7. A Couple Sitting Under a Starry Sky

With this love-filled Valentine’s Day wallpaper from iGeeksBlog, picture you and your partner cuddled under a starry night sky. I’m sure this image can make your partner feel the tender embrace of your arms and the cozy comfort of your love.

Download

8. Couples Kissing Wallpaper

A kiss is a love note whispered upon the lips, conveying the sweetest sentiments that emerge straight from the heart. It’s a magical moment that paints a picture of endless adoration, the perfect backdrop for your Valentine’s Day dream to come true.

Download

9. Snoopy Valentine’s Day

Snoopy’s loving hug provides a magnificent blend of pleasure, laughter, and pure delight. This is what your iPhone needs every time you light it up. Don’t skip a beat! Now is the time to download the wallpaper and give your iPhone a lovely Valentine’s kiss.

Download

10. Anime Heartwarming

Add a love-filled twist as you adorn your iPhone with the most heartwarming Valentine’s Day anime wallpapers starring the characters you hold dear to your heart. Follow the download link and let the love overflow!

Download

11. Wired Heart

May your love for your partner glow like a dazzling wired heart that has stood the test of time. Decorate your iPhone screen with this beautiful Valentine’s Day wallpaper to remind yourself of the power of your relationship. May your love continue to glitter and shine for all time.

Download

12. Butterfly Heart

Butterflies in the stomach and the repetitive thump-thump of a heart in love. Who can forget that first fateful encounter with their beloved? Download this wallpaper and relive those memories!

Download

13. Wild hearts wallpaper

Decorate your iPhone with this lovely Valentine’s Day wallpaper and dive into the ocean of love. Simply click the download button below to get your surprise!

Download

14. Layered love Valentine’s week

Love is like your Apple device; it has multiple layers of security and safety. It’s an ideal complement to your and your sweetheart’s love, just like this wallpaper!

Download

15. Valentine’s Day teddy

Our talented graphic designers have created an adorable Valentine’s Day cute teddy iPhone wallpaper just for you! This heartfelt design is a visual representation of our heartfelt emotions for you. Download this wallpaper and accept our token of appreciation.

Download

Celebrate Valentine’s Day in Style! 

No matter your style, cute, classy, or a little dramatic, the right Valentine’s Day wallpaper can make your iPhone feel extra special. Pick the one that matches your mood, spread a little love, and let your screen celebrate the season too.

Also, don’t forget to check out our other cute, adorable wallpaper collections!

More wallpapers for your iPhone:

  • Beautiful night sky wallpapers for iPhone
  • 10 Cute Grinch wallpapers for iPhone
  • 16 Free Disney wallpapers for iPhone

title.rendered: How to Edit and Annotate PDFs on a Mac (Free and Built-In Tools)

content.rendered:
PDFs are great for sharing documents, but editing them on a Mac can feel confusing at first. You might want to highlight text, fill out a form, add your signature, or rearrange pages, only to find yourself searching for third-party apps.

What many users do not realize is that macOS already includes built-in tools for working with PDFs. Using Preview, Quick Look, and Pages, you can annotate files, complete forms, sign documents, organize pages, and even edit editable PDFs. This guide explains how to edit and annotate PDFs on a Mac using built-in macOS tools.

Table of Contents
  • What macOS Offers for PDF Editing
  • How to Edit and Annotate PDFs in Preview on Mac
    • Rearranging, Rotating, and Deleting Pages
  • How to Fill PDF Forms and Add a Signature on Mac
  • Annotate PDFs Quickly with Quick Look
  • Edit Actual PDF Text Using Pages (If the File Is Editable)
  • What You Can and Cannot Edit on Mac
  • Tips to Improve Your PDF Editing Workflow
  • When You Need a Third-Party PDF Editor
  • Common PDF Editing Problems on Mac
  • Editing PDFs on Mac Made Easy

What macOS Offers for PDF Editing

macOS focuses on simple, practical PDF tools. You can highlight text, add notes, draw shapes, rearrange pages, and sign documents right out of the box. These features cover most everyday needs, such as reviewing files, leaving comments, and preparing documents to share.

For deeper edits, like changing existing text, macOS also offers a lesser-known option in Pages, provided the PDF is editable.

How to Edit and Annotate PDFs in Preview on Mac

Preview is the main PDF workspace on Mac. It is designed for visual edits like highlights, comments, shapes, and page management. This makes it ideal for reviewing documents or adding feedback without altering the original content structure.

  1. Go to Finder and open the PDF file you want to edit or annotate.
  2. Click the Markup icon (pen tip) to reveal annotation tools.
  3. From the toolbar that appears, you can:
    • Highlight or underline text
    • Add text boxes
    • Insert arrows, circles, and rectangles
    • Leave comments
    • Draw freehand using your trackpad or mouse
  4. Once done, press Command + S to save your changes.

Rearranging, Rotating, and Deleting Pages

Preview also lets you manage multi-page PDFs. When you open a multi-page PDF, page thumbnails appear in the left sidebar, making it easy to organize your document visually.

  1. Drag and drop the PDF pages in the sidebar to reorder them.
  2. To delete a page, select and press the Delete key.
  3. You can also rotate pages left or right by clicking Tools → Rotate Left or Rotate Right.

How to Fill PDF Forms and Add a Signature on Mac

Preview allows you to fill out forms and sign documents in one smooth flow. Next to the Markup icon, you will see the Form Filling button. It highlights all interactive fields so you can enter details cleanly before adding your signature.

  1. Open the PDF in Preview.
  2. Click the Form Filling icon to highlight fillable fields.
  3. Now, select each highlighted field to enter your details, such as your name, date, or address.
  4. To add your signature to the PDF:
    • Click the Signature button, and select one of the available signatures.
    • If no signature exists, click the Create Signature button.
    • Next, create your signature by either using the Mac’s trackpad, camera, or iPhone.
    • Click Done.
    • Now add the signature to the PDF, then drag, place, and resize it as needed.

Annotate PDFs Quickly with Quick Look

Quick Look is built for speed. It lets you make small edits directly in Finder without fully opening Preview. This is useful when you need to highlight something or add a quick note before sending a file.

  1. Select the PDF in Finder and press the Spacebar to open it in Quick Look.
  2. Click the Markup icon.
  3. Add highlights, text, or drawings.
  4. Click Done to save.

Edit Actual PDF Text Using Pages (If the File Is Editable)

If a PDF is fully editable and not scanned or flattened, you can open it in Pages to modify the actual content.

Pages converts the PDF into a document format, allowing you to change text, replace images, and adjust formatting. This works best with simple PDFs such as resumes or basic documents.

Note Scanned or image-based PDFs will not open properly in Pages unless they are converted to editable text first.

What You Can and Cannot Edit on Mac

macOS native tools focus on annotation and layout adjustments rather than deep content editing.

Tips to Improve Your PDF Editing Workflow

A few simple habits can make PDF editing smoother:

  • Zoom in before placing text boxes for better alignment.
  • Use different highlight colors to organize feedback.
  • Turn on thumbnails when working with long documents.
  • Duplicate important PDFs before making heavy edits.
  • Use trackpad drawing for quick arrows or circles.

When You Need a Third-Party PDF Editor

While Preview and Pages handle most everyday tasks, advanced workflows may require dedicated tools. Consider third-party apps if you need:

  • Direct paragraph editing in complex PDFs
  • OCR for scanned documents
  • Advanced form creation or editing
  • File compression or format conversion

These tools are better suited for legal, publishing, or document-heavy work.

Common PDF Editing Problems on Mac

Editing PDFs on Mac Made Easy

That’s it. Working with PDFs on a Mac does not have to be complicated. With Preview and Quick Look, you can handle everyday tasks like highlighting text, filling forms, adding signatures, and organizing pages without installing extra software. For editable PDFs, Pages gives you a way to modify actual content when Preview is not enough.

Still stuck with a PDF on Mac? Leave a comment, and we will help you out.

FAQs

Do I need third-party apps to edit PDFs on Mac?

No. Preview, Quick Look, and Pages handle most tasks such as annotations, form filling, signatures, and page management. Third-party apps are only needed for OCR or advanced text editing.

Where are my saved signatures stored in macOS?

macOS saves your signature automatically and shows it in Preview whenever you use the Signature tool. You do not need to recreate it.

How do I add comments or notes to a PDF on a Mac?

Open the PDF in Preview, click Markup, then use Notes or Text Box. You can also add quick comments through Quick Look.

mainEntity.name: Do I need third-party apps to edit PDFs on Mac?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Preview, Quick Look, and Pages handle most tasks such as annotations, form filling, signatures, and page management. Third-party apps are only needed for OCR or advanced text editing.

mainEntity.name: Where are my saved signatures stored in macOS?

acceptedAnswer.text: macOS saves your signature automatically and shows it in Preview whenever you use the Signature tool. You do not need to recreate it.

mainEntity.name: How do I add comments or notes to a PDF on a Mac?

acceptedAnswer.text: Open the PDF in Preview, click Markup, then use Notes or Text Box. You can also add quick comments through Quick Look.

title.rendered: Apple Pay Not Working on iPhone? Here’s How to Fix It

content.rendered:
Apple Pay is a fast, secure, and convenient way to pay using your iPhone. So when it suddenly stops working, it can be frustrating, especially if you are at a checkout counter or trying to complete an urgent payment.

The good news is that most Apple Pay issues are easy to fix. In this guide, you will learn why Apple Pay may not be working on your iPhone and how to fix it step by step using simple, practical solutions.

Table of Contents
  • Why Apple Pay Is Not Working on Your iPhone
  • Quick Checks Before You Start Troubleshooting
  • Easy Fixes to Try First for Apple Pay Issues
    • Restart Your iPhone
    • Check Your Internet Connection
    • Check Apple System Status
  • Apple Pay Settings You Should Check on iPhone
    • Verify the Default Card
    • Re-authenticate Face ID or Touch ID
  • Fix Card-Related Problems in Apple Pay
    • Choose a Card Manually
    • Remove and Re-Add the Card
    • Contact Your Bank or Card Issuer
  • Fix Apple Pay Issues Caused by iOS or System Bugs
    • Update iOS
    • Disable Low Power Mode
    • Sign Out and Sign Back Into Apple ID
    • Reset Network Settings
  • Apple Pay Not Working in Stores vs Online Payments
    • Apple Pay Not Working at POS Terminals
    • Apple Pay Not Working in Apps or Websites
  • Advanced Apple Pay Troubleshooting (Last Resort)
  • Final Thoughts

Why Apple Pay Is Not Working on Your iPhone

Apple Pay can fail for several reasons, and it is not always obvious which one is causing the problem.

Here are the most common causes:

  • Device compatibility issues: Older iPhone models do not support Apple Pay because they lack NFC and secure authentication.
  • Internet or network problems: Apple Pay requires an internet connection for online and in-app purchases.
  • Card or bank-related restrictions: Your bank may block transactions, suspend the card, or not fully support Apple Pay.
  • Software glitches or outdated iOS: Bugs or older iOS versions can disrupt Apple Pay functionality.
  • Incorrect settings: If Apple Pay is not set up correctly, payments may fail.
  • Region, merchant, or payment terminal issues: Not all countries, stores, or terminals support Apple Pay, even if the logo is visible.

Quick Checks Before You Start Troubleshooting

Before trying advanced fixes, rule out basic limitations.

  • Confirm Apple Pay is supported in your country or region: Apple Pay is not available everywhere, and some regions limit certain card types. Check if your location is supported.
  • Check if the merchant accepts Apple Pay: Look for the Apple Pay or contactless symbol at checkout.
  • Make sure your device supports Apple Pay: iPhones with Face ID or Touch ID, except iPhone 5s, are required.
  • Verify your card is eligible and active: Expired, suspended, or unsupported cards will not work.
  • Enable required security features: Face ID, Touch ID, or a passcode must be enabled, along with two-factor authentication for your Apple Account.

Easy Fixes to Try First for Apple Pay Issues

Before changing advanced settings or contacting your bank, start with these simple fixes. They solve many Apple Pay problems.

Restart Your iPhone

Restarting clears temporary system glitches that may interfere with Apple Pay.

  1. Long press the Side and Volume button of your iPhone.
  2. You will see a power off slider. Drag it to the right.
  3. Wait for a few seconds and turn on your iPhone.
  4. After the phone boots up, try using Apple Pay again.

Check Your Internet Connection

Apple Pay needs a stable internet connection, especially for online and in-app purchases. Even in stores, your iPhone may need to communicate with Apple servers or your bank.

  • Switch between Wi-Fi and mobile data.
  • Turn Airplane Mode on for a few seconds, then turn it off.
  • Avoid weak or restricted networks, such as public Wi-Fi that blocks secure transactions.

Check Apple System Status

Occasionally, Apple Pay issues are caused by temporary service outages.

Apple Pay relies on backend services for payment processing and authentication. If these services are down, payments may fail.

Check Apple’s System Status page to see if Apple Pay, Wallet, or iCloud services are unavailable. If there is an outage, you will need to wait until it is resolved.

Apple Pay Settings You Should Check on iPhone

If Apple Pay still does not work, review your settings carefully. Small misconfigurations can cause failures, especially after updates.

Verify the Default Card

Apple Pay uses your default card automatically.

  1. Go to Settings > Wallet & Apple Pay.
  2. Select Apple Pay Defaults.
  3. Here, verify all the details and settings.

If the default card is blocked or over its limit, payments may fail even if other cards are available.

Re-authenticate Face ID or Touch ID

Apple Pay requires biometric authentication to complete payments.

  1. Open Settings and select Face ID & Passcode (or Touch ID & Passcode).
  2. Enter your device passcode.
  3. Make sure the Contactless & Payments toggle is enabled.

If Face ID or Touch ID has been unreliable, turn it off, restart your iPhone, and set it up again.

Fix Card-Related Problems in Apple Pay

If Apple Pay opens but transactions keep getting declined, the issue is often related to the card.

Choose a Card Manually

If your default card keeps failing, try another one.

  1. Double-click the side button of your iPhone and authenticate your Face ID to open the Wallet interface.
  2. Tap your default card. It will show you other saved card.
  3. Choose a different card and again verify your identity.
  4. Finally, hold your iPhone near the payment terminal.
Tip Credit cards usually work more reliably than debit cards, especially for online or international payments.

Remove and Re-Add the Card

Removing and re-adding a card can fix hidden verification issues.

  1. Open the Wallet app and choose the card that’s causing problems.
  2. Tap the the three-dot icon and select Card Details.
  3. Scroll down and tap Remove Card. Verify your Face ID to confirm.
  4. Go back to Wallet app homepage and tap the plus icon.
  5. Select your card type and follow the on-screen instructions to verify and add the card.

This refreshes the secure payment token used by Apple Pay.

If you are facing issues when adding cards, go through this guide for card-related fixes.

Contact Your Bank or Card Issuer

Sometimes the issue is entirely on the bank’s side. Banks may block Apple Pay due to:

  • Suspected fraud
  • Travel or international usage
  • Large or repeated payments
  • Apple Pay being disabled on your account

A quick call or chat with your bank can often resolve the issue within minutes.

Fix Apple Pay Issues Caused by iOS or System Bugs

If settings and cards look fine, the issue may be related to iOS.

Update iOS

Outdated iOS versions can cause Apple Pay to stop working.

  1. Go to Settings > General > Software Update and install any available updates.
  2. After updating, restart your iPhone before trying Apple Pay again.
Tip Make sure Date & Time is set to automatic.

Disable Low Power Mode

Low Power Mode can limit background processes that Apple Pay depends on.

  1. Open Settings > Battery.
  2. Turn off Low Power Mode.
  3. Lock and unlock your iPhone, then try Apple Pay again.

Sign Out and Sign Back Into Apple ID

Apple Pay relies on your Apple ID for authentication.

  1. Go to Settings and tap your name at the top.
  2. Scroll down and tap Sign Out.
  3. It will show you a prompt. Select Sign Out But Don’t Erase > Continue.
  4. Follow the instructions to sign out of your Apple Account safely.
  5. Restart your iPhone.
  6. Now, sign back in using the same Apple ID email address and password.

Check Wallet to confirm your cards are still available.

Reset Network Settings

Network issues can interfere with Apple Pay.

  1. Go to Settings > General > Transfer or Reset iPhone.
  2. Tap Reset and Reset Network Settings.
  3. Enter your passcode.

Reconnect to Wi-Fi or mobile data and test Apple Pay again.

Apple Pay Not Working in Stores vs Online Payments

Apple Pay issues often depend on where you’re trying to pay.

Apple Pay Not Working at POS Terminals

  • NFC issues: Make sure NFC is working properly.
  • Phone positioning tips: Hold the top of your iPhone close to the payment terminal for a few seconds.
  • Remove phone case: Thick or metal cases can interfere with NFC signals.
  • Traveling abroad? Currency rules or international transaction blocks may stop Apple Pay from working.

Check out our guide to learn which stores accept Apple Pay.

Apple Pay Not Working in Apps or Websites

  • App compatibility issues: Some apps don’t fully support Apple Pay or need updates.
  • Safari vs third-party browsers: Apple Pay works best in Safari. Many third-party browsers don’t support it.

Advanced Apple Pay Troubleshooting (Last Resort)

If nothing else works, try these only as a last step.

  • Reset All Settings: This resets system preferences without deleting data.
  • Erase and Restore iPhone: Always back up your iPhone first. This completely refreshes the system.
  • Contact Apple Support: If Apple Pay still doesn’t work, official support can check hardware or account-level issues.

Final Thoughts

Apple Pay not working on your iPhone can be frustrating, but most issues are easy to fix.

If problems continue, contact your bank or Apple Support. In many cases, the issue is related to security restrictions rather than your device.

Which solution worked for you? Share your experience in the comments.

FAQs

Why does Apple Pay say “Payment Not Completed”?

This usually happens due to network issues, bank restrictions, or Apple service outages.

Why is Apple Pay declined but my physical card works?

Apple Pay uses virtual card numbers, which banks may block even if the physical card works.

Can Apple Pay stop working after an update?

Yes. iOS updates can introduce bugs, which are usually fixed in later updates.

mainEntity.name: Do I need third-party apps to edit PDFs on Mac?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Preview, Quick Look, and Pages handle most tasks such as annotations, form filling, signatures, and page management. Third-party apps are only needed for OCR or advanced text editing.

mainEntity.name: Where are my saved signatures stored in macOS?

acceptedAnswer.text: macOS saves your signature automatically and shows it in Preview whenever you use the Signature tool. You do not need to recreate it.

mainEntity.name: How do I add comments or notes to a PDF on a Mac?

acceptedAnswer.text: Open the PDF in Preview, click Markup, then use Notes or Text Box. You can also add quick comments through Quick Look.

mainEntity.name: Why does Apple Pay say “Payment Not Completed”?

acceptedAnswer.text: This usually happens due to network issues, bank restrictions, or Apple service outages.

mainEntity.name: Why is Apple Pay declined but my physical card works?

acceptedAnswer.text: Apple Pay uses virtual card numbers, which banks may block even if the physical card works.

mainEntity.name: Can Apple Pay stop working after an update?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. iOS updates can introduce bugs, which are usually fixed in later updates.

title.rendered: How to Use Live Text on iPhone to Copy, Translate, and Look Up Text

content.rendered:
If you have ever wanted your iPhone to copy and interact with text from images and videos in real time, recognize phone numbers from a sign, or instantly translate a sentence captured with your camera, Apple’s Live Text makes it possible. It turns your iPhone into a powerful text recognition tool that works quickly and intelligently.

Whether you are a student, traveler, or professional, this feature helps you get more done with less effort. In this guide, you will learn how to use Live Text to copy text from photos and videos on your iPhone, along with practical tips to get the most out of it.

Table of Contents
  • What Is Live Text on iPhone and How Does It Work?
    • How Live Text Works
    • Supported Languages and Content Types
  • How to Enable Live Text on iPhone
  • How to Use Live Text on iPhone
    • Using Live Text in the Camera App
    • Using Live Text in the Photos App
    • Using Live Text in Safari, Mail, and Other Apps
  • Live Text Actions You Can Perform
  • What is the Difference Between Live Text and Visual Look Up?
  • Tips and Tricks for Using Live Text Effectively
  • Common Problems and How to Fix Them
  • Final Thoughts

What Is Live Text on iPhone and How Does It Work?

Live Text is an Apple feature that lets your iPhone detect and interact with text from images and the live camera viewfinder. It uses on-device intelligence to understand what is in front of you and offers actionable options such as copying text, calling a phone number, or translating foreign language text.

How Live Text Works

Live Text uses on-device machine learning and OCR (optical character recognition). This means your iPhone can read text without sending data to the cloud, making it fast and privacy focused.

When text appears in your camera view or in a photo:

  • A Live Text indicator appears
  • You can tap to interact with detected text
  • Your iPhone highlights recognized letters and numbers

You no longer need to manually type text from signs, menus, or screenshots. Live Text lets you instantly copy long paragraphs, saving time and reducing errors.

Supported Languages and Content Types

Similar to Google Lens, Live Text can recognize:

  • Printed text such as books, signs, and posters
  • Handwriting, especially neat or block writing
  • Numbers including phone numbers, prices, and dates
  • URLs and email addresses
  • Physical addresses

Live Text supports multiple languages, and recognition improves with each iOS update. It works best when your region and language settings match the text you are scanning.

How to Enable Live Text on iPhone

Before using Live Text, make sure the following requirements are met:

  • Your iPhone is running iOS 15 or later. Updating to the latest iOS version is recommended.
  • You are using a supported model with an A12 Bionic chip or newer.
  • Live Text is enabled in Settings.

Steps to Enable Live Text:

  1. Open Settings.
  2. Tap General > Language & Region.
  3. Make sure Live Text is turned on.
  4. Go back to the main Settings screen and select Camera.
  5. Turn on Show Detected Text.

If you do not see these options, your iPhone model or iOS version may not support Live Text.

How to Use Live Text on iPhone

Live Text works across the system, including the Camera app, Photos app, and supported apps like Safari and Mail.

Using Live Text in the Camera App

  1. Open the Camera app.
  2. Point at text (a sign, document, page).
  3. Look for the Live Text icon in the bottom right corner.
  4. Tap the icon to capture text in between the yellow box.
  5. Now, tap and hold the text to highlight it.
  6. Choose actions like Copy, Look Up, Translate, etc.

Using Live Text in the Photos App

  1. Open the Photos app.
  2. Tap a photo containing text.
  3. Tap the Live Text icon in the bottom right corner.
  4. All recognized text will be highlighted. If the image includes a phone number or foreign language text, you may see action buttons such as Call or Translate.
  5. To interact with specific text, tap and hold it. You can then tap the arrow icon in the floating menu to access options like Copy, Writing Tools, Look Up, or Search Web.

Live Text also works with videos. Pause the video at any frame and select the text. The feature is available on Mac as well, so you can use it across Apple devices.

Using Live Text in Safari, Mail, and Other Apps

Live Text works inside supported apps:

  • In Safari, tap and hold an image and select Show Text. It will launch the Live Text interface. Now you can copy, translate, or Look Up for it.
  • In Mail and Messages, tap and hold on the text from photos to interact.

The experience is consistent across apps. If you can see text, Live Text can usually detect it.

Live Text Actions You Can Perform

Live Text offers more than simple copy and paste:

  • Copy and paste text from images into any app
  • Translate text instantly into your system language
  • Look up addresses and directions in Maps
  • Call phone numbers or email contacts with a single tap
  • Search the web using detected text
  • Track flights using flight numbers in images
  • Convert currency into your local format
  • Add events to Calendar when dates or times are detected
  • Track shipments using recognized tracking numbers

What is the Difference Between Live Text and Visual Look Up?

Although they often work together, Live Text and Visual Look Up serve different purposes:

  • Live Text focuses on detecting and interacting with text.
  • Visual Look Up identifies objects, animals, landmarks, artwork, and more.

Use Live Text when you want to read or interact with text. Use Visual Look Up when you want more information about objects in an image.

Tips and Tricks for Using Live Text Effectively

  • Use good lighting and focus for better accuracy.
  • Keep handwriting clear and neat for reliable recognition.
  • Add multiple languages in Settings > General > Language & Region if you frequently scan foreign text.

Common Problems and How to Fix Them

If Live Text is not working on your iPhone, try these solutions:

Final Thoughts

Live Text may seem like a small feature, but once you start using it, it becomes a daily productivity booster. It turns your iPhone into a powerful text reader, and after a while, it is hard to imagine using your phone without it.

Have you tried Live Text yet? Share your experience in the comments.

FAQs

Does Live Text work offline?

Yes. Live Text works offline because text recognition happens on the device. However, features like web search may require an internet connection.

Can Live Text recognize handwriting?

Yes. It works best with neat and clearly written handwriting.

Can Live Text extract text from PDFs?

Yes. Open the PDF in the Photos or Files app and use Live Text to interact with the text.

mainEntity.name: Do I need third-party apps to edit PDFs on Mac?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Preview, Quick Look, and Pages handle most tasks such as annotations, form filling, signatures, and page management. Third-party apps are only needed for OCR or advanced text editing.

mainEntity.name: Where are my saved signatures stored in macOS?

acceptedAnswer.text: macOS saves your signature automatically and shows it in Preview whenever you use the Signature tool. You do not need to recreate it.

mainEntity.name: How do I add comments or notes to a PDF on a Mac?

acceptedAnswer.text: Open the PDF in Preview, click Markup, then use Notes or Text Box. You can also add quick comments through Quick Look.

title.rendered: Apple’s CarPlay Ultra Is Finally Expanding Beyond Luxury Cars

content.rendered:
Apple is getting ready to expand CarPlay Ultra beyond its current exclusivity with Aston Martin, with more mainstream vehicles expected to arrive in the second half of 2026.

According to Mark Gurman’s Power On newsletter for Bloomberg, at least one major model from either Hyundai or Kia is set to gain CarPlay Ultra later this year. Apple has previously confirmed that Genesis is also part of its rollout plans.

What CarPlay Ultra Brings to Your Dashboard

Unlike standard CarPlay, CarPlay Ultra takes control of multiple screens inside the vehicle. It blends iPhone-powered apps with real-time vehicle data, including speed, fuel level, battery status, tire pressure, and engine temperature.

Drivers also get native interfaces for climate controls, radio functions, and rear camera feeds, all designed to match each automaker’s visual style. Users can choose from multiple layout presets, allowing for a more personalized dashboard experience.

Other Automakers are Still Hesitant

Not every car brand is eager to embrace Apple’s deeper in-car integration. BMW, Ford, and Rivian have publicly played down interest in CarPlay Ultra.

General Motors has gone even further, removing standard CarPlay from its newer EV lineup. This move effectively rules out CarPlay Ultra for brands such as Chevrolet, Cadillac, and GMC.

Tesla also appears unlikely to support CarPlay Ultra, although reports suggest the company may reconsider adding standard CarPlay support in the future.

What This Means Going Forward

If Hyundai or Kia launches CarPlay Ultra later this year, it would mark Apple’s first serious push toward mass-market adoption. That shift would give buyers outside the luxury segment their first look at Apple’s fully integrated in-car experience, with other brands likely to follow once the rollout gains momentum.

Would you want CarPlay Ultra in your next car? Let us know in the comments.

  • His passion for technology and Apple products led him to iGeeksBlog, where he specializes in writing How-to and troubleshooting guides for fellow Apple enthusiasts.

Experience

title.rendered: Wi-Fi Privacy Warning on iPhone: What It Means and How to Fix It

content.rendered:
Seeing a Wi-Fi Privacy Warning pop up on your iPhone can feel unsettling. You connect to your usual network, everything loads fine, yet Apple suddenly warns you about privacy. Most people feel confused and start wondering whether something is wrong with their iPhone or if their data is at risk. This message appears when your iPhone detects insecure Wi-Fi settings that could expose your online activity. Fortunately, with the right steps, you can fix it in just a few minutes.

This guide explains what the Wi-Fi Privacy Warning means, why it appears, and how to get rid of it so you can browse safely again.

Table of Contents
  • What Does the Wi-Fi Privacy Warning Mean on iPhone?
  • Why Your iPhone Shows a Wi-Fi Privacy Warning
  • Is It Safe to Use Wi-Fi With a Privacy Warning?
  • How to Fix Wi-Fi Privacy Warning on iPhone
    • 1. Turn On Private Wi-Fi Address
    • 2. Forget and Reconnect to the Network
    • 3. Restart Your iPhone and Router
    • 4. Update iOS to the Latest Version
    • 5. Reset Network Settings
    • 6. Check and Fix Router Security Settings
  • Tips to Stay Safe on Public Wi-Fi With an iPhone
  • Stay Safe on Wi-Fi

What Does the Wi-Fi Privacy Warning Mean on iPhone?

A Wi-Fi Privacy Warning appears when your iPhone connects to a wireless network that uses weak or outdated security, or when important privacy features such as Private Wi-Fi Address are turned off.

Apple displays this alert to let you know the network could allow others to view your activity, intercept data, or track your device. While the warning does not always mean the network is malicious, it does indicate that your connection is not fully protected.

Why Your iPhone Shows a Wi-Fi Privacy Warning

Your iPhone may display a Wi-Fi Privacy Warning for several reasons, including:

  • The router uses older security standards, such as WEP, or an unsecured open network
  • Private Wi-Fi Address is disabled for that network
  • The router configuration is incomplete or outdated
  • You are connected to public Wi-Fi at airports, cafes, hotels, or malls
  • Your router firmware has not been updated in a long time

Is It Safe to Use Wi-Fi With a Privacy Warning?

Technically, yes. You can still use the internet for basic everyday activities. However, it is not recommended for sensitive tasks such as online banking, signing into important accounts, or sharing personal information.

When you see this warning, treat the network as insecure and either fix the issue or switch to mobile data until it is resolved.

How to Fix Wi-Fi Privacy Warning on iPhone

Now that you know why your iPhone shows the Wi-Fi Privacy Warning, here’s how you can fix it.

1. Turn On Private Wi-Fi Address

Private Wi-Fi Address is enabled by default on all iPhones and is usually set to Fixed for most networks. This means your iPhone uses the same private address for that Wi-Fi network unless you change it. While this works fine in most cases, some routers struggle with this setup and may trigger the Wi-Fi Privacy Warning.

Follow these steps:

  1. Open Settings → Wi-Fi.
  2. Tap the i button next to the connected network.
  3. Tap Private Wi-Fi Address.
  4. You will see three options:
    • Off
    • Fixed (default)
    • Rotate
  5. Select Rotating, then go back, disconnect from the network, and reconnect.

This allows your iPhone to periodically change its private address, which can clear the warning on certain networks.

2. Forget and Reconnect to the Network

Your iPhone saves Wi-Fi networks and reconnects automatically. Sometimes, the stored network profile becomes outdated after router changes, password updates, or iOS upgrades. When that happens, your iPhone may continue using old settings and trigger the privacy warning.

Forgetting the network removes those saved details and forces your iPhone to create a fresh connection.

  1. Open Settings → Wi-Fi.
  2. Tap the i button next to the connected network.
  3. Tap Forget This Network and confirm

Restart your iPhone, then reconnect to the network by entering the password again. This often resolves the issue.

3. Restart Your iPhone and Router

Both your iPhone and router often run continuously for weeks or months, which can lead to minor connection glitches. Even if Wi-Fi appears to work, background network services may be stuck.

Restarting your iPhone refreshes its network processes. Restarting your router clears temporary routing issues and refreshes connection data.

4. Update iOS to the Latest Version

iOS updates do more than add new features. Apple also improves Wi-Fi security handling and fixes bugs related to network detection. If your iPhone is running an older version of iOS, it may incorrectly flag secure networks or fail to negotiate modern encryption.

  1. Go to Settings → General → Software Update.
  2. Install any available update.

After updating, reconnect to Wi-Fi and check whether the warning is gone.

5. Reset Network Settings

If the warning still appears, resetting network settings can help.

Your iPhone stores Wi-Fi configurations, DNS data, VPN profiles, and cellular settings in the background. Over time, these can conflict with router changes or new networks. Resetting network settings clears all of this without deleting your apps or personal data.

  1. Go to Settings → General → Transfer or Reset iPhone.
  2. Tap Reset Network Settings.
  3. Tap Reset.

6. Check and Fix Router Security Settings

If the warning keeps returning on your home Wi-Fi, the issue is likely with your router. Modern routers should use WPA2 or WPA3 encryption, but older routers or custom configurations may still rely on weaker security standards. Even password-protected networks can trigger Apple’s privacy warning if encryption is outdated.

To fix this:

  1. Log in to your router’s admin panel using its IP address in Safari.
  2. Set Wi-Fi security to WPA2 or WPA3.
  3. Avoid open networks or WEP encryption.
  4. Update the router firmware if an update is available.

Tips to Stay Safe on Public Wi-Fi With an iPhone

Even with Apple’s strong privacy protections, public Wi-Fi networks still carry risks. To stay safe:

  • Keep Private Wi-Fi Address enabled.
  • Avoid banking or work accounts on public Wi-Fi.
  • Use a trusted VPN for added protection.
  • Forget public networks after use.
  • Keep your iPhone updated to the latest iOS version.

Stay Safe on Wi-Fi

A Wi-Fi Privacy Warning on iPhone is Apple’s way of alerting you to potentially insecure networks. While it may look serious, it is usually easy to fix. If the warning persists even after trying all the steps above, it is best to disconnect from that network for now.

If this guide helped you, feel free to leave a comment and share what worked for you.

Explore more…

  • Ways to boost Wi-Fi signal on iPhone and iPad
  • Wi-Fi not working on iPhone? Fix it!
  • Wi-Fi keeps switching to cellular on iPhone? Fix it!

mainEntity.name: Do I need third-party apps to edit PDFs on Mac?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Preview, Quick Look, and Pages handle most tasks such as annotations, form filling, signatures, and page management. Third-party apps are only needed for OCR or advanced text editing.

title.rendered: Apple May Be Working on a Flip-Style Foldable iPhone

content.rendered:
Apple is quietly exploring a new foldable iPhone design that would fold in half like a flip phone, according to recent reporting. The idea is still in the early stages, but it suggests Apple is thinking beyond a single foldable model as it prepares to enter the foldable phone market.

The concept was mentioned in the latest Power On newsletter, which says Apple is considering a square, clamshell-style foldable phone inside its development labs. While there is no confirmation the product will ever ship, the exploration signals Apple’s interest in expanding the iPhone lineup with new form factors over time.

A Smaller Foldable Could Follow Apple’s First Foldable iPhone

Apple’s immediate focus remains on its first foldable iPhone, which is expected to debut later this year with a book-style folding design. That device is widely seen as Apple’s initial test of consumer demand for foldable smartphones.

If the first model proves successful, Apple believes customers may want additional options, much like they do with today’s slab-style iPhones. A clamshell foldable would offer a more compact alternative, designed for users who prefer portability without giving up a full-size smartphone experience.

Apple Has Considered This Design Before

This is not the first time Apple has explored a flip-style foldable iPhone. In previous years, the company reportedly built multiple clamshell prototypes while evaluating how it should approach foldable hardware.

Apple ultimately prioritized a larger foldable design, but the renewed interest in a clamshell form factor suggests the company continues to revisit earlier concepts as technology matures and market conditions evolve.

What This Says About Apple’s Foldable Strategy

There is no release timeline for a clamshell foldable iPhone, and there is no guarantee it will ever reach consumers. Apple routinely tests products internally without committing them to production.

Still, the discussion highlights a broader strategy taking shape. Apple appears to be planning for a future where the iPhone lineup includes multiple foldable designs, offering different sizes and use cases rather than a single experimental device.

excerpt.rendered: Apple may be working on a flip-style foldable iPhone that folds in half like a classic clamshell phone. The idea is still in early development, but it suggests Apple is already thinking beyond its first foldable iPhone as it prepares for a broader foldable future.

title.rendered: Best iPhone Power Banks for Travel, Work, and Everyday Use

content.rendered:
Running low on battery can disrupt your entire day. To avoid this inconvenience, it’s wise to invest in a good power bank that can keep your phone charged anytime, anywhere. Whether you’re traveling, commuting, or working on the go, a portable power bank ensures you stay connected whenever needed.

However, it’s crucial to choose the right product that can serve you well. So in this article, I’ve rounded up the best power banks for iPhone that are tried and tested to offer reliable performance. Check out my top recommendations below.

Table of Contents
  • What to consider when choosing a power bank for your iPhone
  • What is the best power bank to use with an iPhone?
    • 1. Anker PowerCore – Best overall iPhone power bank
    • 2. Belkin – High capacity 20,000mAh power bank
    • 3. TORRAS – Best MagSafe power bank
    • 4. Miiso – Stylish and compact portable charger
    • 5. Belkin BOOSTCHARGE – Portable charger with built-in cables
    • 6. Anker 633 – Wireless power bank with stand
    • 7. TORRAS -Ultra compact power bank
  • Signing off…

What to consider when choosing a power bank for your iPhone

Here are the key factors to consider before spending your money on a portable charger for your iPhone:

  • Capacity: A power bank’s capacity is measured in milliampere-hours (mAh), and determines how many times it can charge your iPhone. A power bank with a capacity of 5,000mAh is ideal for a single charge, while options with 10,000mAh or more can provide multiple charges, making them perfect for heavy users or travelers.
  • Ports: Different power banks offer various types and numbers of ports, so it’s essential to check compatibility. It’s best to get one that has multiple types of ports with at least one USB-C port as this often provides the fastest charging experience. Moreover, if the power bank has built-in charging cables, make sure the cable matches your iPhone port. So, if you have an iPhone 15 or later, there should be a USB-C charging cable. Older iPhones require a Lightning cable.
  • MagSafe Compatibility: If you own a MagSafe-compatible iPhone, a MagSafe power bank may be a good option. These magnetically attach to the back of your device, eliminating the need for cables and offering a seamless charging experience on the go.
  • Charging Speed: Not all power banks charge at the same speed. Look for models that support fast charging, such as 18W or higher as this can significantly reduce the time it takes to get your device back to 100%. Note that wireless power banks typically offer slower charging than wired ones.
  • Portability: While higher-capacity power banks are useful, they tend to be bulkier. If you’re looking for something you can easily slip into your pocket or bag, prioritize slim, lightweight options.

When creating this guide, we’ve kept all these important criteria in mind to provide you with a variety of power bank options to match your preferences.

At iGeeksBlog, we take our time to test out products before recommending them. Our team of experts is committed to ensuring that you get value for your money and you can trust us for unbiased and authentic information. To know more about our process, read about how we test products.

What is the best power bank to use with an iPhone?

Based on our tests and the important criteria described above, here’s our selection of the best power banks for your iPhone.

1. Anker PowerCore – Best overall iPhone power bank

This Anker power bank for iPhone is my favorite for many reasons. To start with, it’s compact yet powerful. The 10,000mAh battery can provide multiple charges, depending on your device, and its sleek and lightweight design makes it an excellent travel companion.

With features like PowerIQ technology and a sturdy build, this power bank balances portability, efficiency, and reliability. It boasts scratch resistance and can withstand drops of up to 3.2 ft, ensuring reliable performance on the go. Moreover, it’s equipped with advanced safety mechanisms like overcharge and short-circuit protection.

Pros

  • Easy to carry in a pocket or bag
  • Sufficient power for multiple charges
  • Efficient charging speeds
  • Durable build quality
  • Affordable price
  • 18-month warranty

Cons

  • It takes quite a long to charge the power bank

Price: 23.99

2. Belkin – High capacity 20,000mAh power bank

Belkin is a trusted brand for iPhone accessories so this power bank does not disappoint. It can charge up to 3 devices simultaneously delivering 78 hours of additional battery life to your iPhone.

It features 2 USB-A ports and a USB-C port. It can charge 2 devices via USB-C at 15W max (shared) and another device via USB-A at 12W max, making it compatible with a wide range of devices including headphones, smartwatches, etc. I especially appreciate the small LED indicator that lets you know the charge level without being intrusive.

Pros

  • Large capacity
  • Sleek design
  • LED power indicator
  • 2-year warranty

Cons

  • Limited Fast Charging Speed

Price: $34.38

3. TORRAS – Best MagSafe power bank

If you prefer a wireless power bank for iPhone, here’s a great option from TORRAS. It’s super compact and portable, packing 5,000mAh of power. This MagSafe accessory attaches securely to the back of your iPhone so that you can enjoy a cable-free charging experience.

Despite its smaller capacity, it provides reliable charging while ensuring protection against overheating and overcharging. Of course, this is not the power bank for multiple charges but it’s a quick and nifty solution when you just need a bit of a battery boost. Moreover, it’s quite high on style with attractive color options of gold, pink, and grey.

Pros

  • MagSafe compatible
  • Compact and lightweight
  • Sleek and attractive design

Cons

  • Relatively low capacity
  • A bit pricey

Price: $42.99

4. Miiso – Stylish and compact portable charger

If you’re looking for the added benefit of not having to carry around a charging cable with your power bank, this option from Miisso is perfect. It boasts built-in USB-C and Lightning cables to charge any iPhone in an instant. The 6,000mAh capacity is enough to provide about one charge for most iPhones.

At the same time, it’s compact and lightweight to carry around. This makes it an excellent choice for everyday use or short trips. Moreover, it has a pretty quick charge time of about 2.5-3 hours ensuring you’re always ready for your next adventure or business trip. This power bank comes in a wide variety of color options to match your unique style.

Pros

  • Built-in cables
  • Ultra lightweight and compact
  • Quick charge time
  • Variety of color options

Cons

  • Charging speed could be better

Price: $30.99

5. Belkin BOOSTCHARGE – Portable charger with built-in cables

Here’s another best-rated portable iPhone charger with built-in cables. Belkin’s BOOSTCHARGE is on the pricier end of the spectrum but I think it’s worth it, given the quality you get. With a 10,000mAh capacity, it provides up to 31 hours of additional battery life for your iPhone or other compatible devices.

The integrated Lightning and USB-C cables eliminate the need to carry separate cables and the 23W output allows you to charge two devices simultaneously. You can enjoy the convenience of charging your device at up to 18W. You can buy with peace of mind because Belkin offers a 2-year limited warranty.

Pros

  • Built-in USB-C and Lightning cables
  • Fast charging speeds
  • Slim design
  • 2-year warranty

Cons

  • Quite pricey
  • Cable quality could be better at this price point

Price: $66.42

6. Anker 633 – Wireless power bank with stand

Here’s a truly unique wireless charger that’s a great investment. This 2-in-1 device charges your compatible iPhone wirelessly while offering a foldable stand for hands-free viewing.
It boasts an ample 10,000mAh lithium-polymer battery that can fully charge an iPhone 13 Pro or later nearly twice on a single charge.

Moreover, it’s MagSafe-compatible, securely aligning with your iPhone to provide reliable wireless charging. It’s available in black, white, and blue color options. You get a 2-year warranty so you can rest assured about quality and durability.

Pros

  • Includes a stand for hands-free viewing
  • MagSafe-compatible
  • Efficient charging

Cons

  • A bit bulky

Price: $54.99

7. TORRAS -Ultra compact power bank

For the minimalists out there, you can’t go wrong with this tiny power bank that still packs a punch. The built-in USB-C connector plugs directly into your iPhone 15 or later, eliminating the need for charging cables. Keep in mind that this power bank will not work with older iPhones that have Lightning ports.

The great part is you can continue to hold your iPhone as usual while this nifty power bank is charging it. It’s lightweight and plugs in securely. It charges your phone from 0% to 50% in about 30 minutes, Being just the size of lipstick, this is a quick-fix charging solution that you can carry anywhere and use on the go.

Pros

  • Small and lightweight
  • No cables required
  • Unobtrusive design

Cons

  • Tends to heat up when in use

Price: $39.98

Signing off…

I hope this guide has helped you pick the best power bank for your iPhone from the wide variety of options available. Now, just remember to keep your power bank charged so that it’s ready to use when you need it! Don’t forget to check out our list of the best fast chargers for iPhone that will add ease and convenience to your life.

  • Best Apple Watch chargers, power banks, stands and docks
  • How to fast charge your iPhone and iPad
  • Best GaN chargers for iPhone, iPad, and Mac

title.rendered: How to Dial an Extension on iPhone: A Complete Guide

content.rendered:
Ever called a bank, office, hospital, or customer care line and heard, “Please enter the extension number now” and then wondered what to do next on your iPhone? You’re not alone. Dialing an extension isn’t difficult, but the option isn’t always obvious if you’ve never done it before.

In this guide, you’ll learn the easiest ways to dial an extension on your iPhone both manually and automatically, save time and avoid frustrating call transfers.

Table of Contents
  • What Is a Phone Extension?
  • Method 1: Dial an Extension Manually on an iPhone
  • Method 2: Save a Phone Number With an Extension on iPhone (Using Pause)
  • Method 3: Use “Wait” for Interactive Voice Menus (IVR Systems)
  • What is the Difference Between Pause and Wait on iPhone?
  • How to Add Multiple Pauses or Waits
  • How to Dial an Extension Automatically on iPhone
  • Troubleshooting: Phone Extension Not Working on iPhone?
  • Final Thoughts

What Is a Phone Extension?

A phone extension is a short internal number used inside a large phone system.

Instead of giving every employee a completely different phone number, companies use:

  • One main phone number
  • Multiple extensions that route calls to different people or departments

For example, you call 1800-123-4567 (main number), then enter 204 (extension).
Your call goes directly to a specific person or desk.

Extensions are common in offices, hospitals, universities, government departments, and customer support centers. So, if you often call them, it’s important to know the iPhone extension dialing guide.

Method 1: Dial an Extension Manually on an iPhone

This is best for one-time calls. If you don’t know the extension for the department you want to reach, first call the number, listen to the automated system, and enter the code using the on-call keyboard.

  1. Open the Phone app.
  2. Tap the Keypad at the bottom.
  3. Dial the main phone number.
  4. Now, tap and hold the asterisk sign (*) until a comma appears.
  5. Enter the extension number using the keypad.
  6. Tap the Call button.

That’s it. The system will connect your call.

Method 2: Save a Phone Number With an Extension on iPhone (Using Pause)

If you call the same number often, save it with the extension so your iPhone dials it for you. This method uses something called Pause, represented by a comma (,).

It tells your iPhone to:

  • Dial the main number
  • Wait for 2 seconds
  • Then automatically dial the extension

Steps to add a Pause:

  1. Open the Contacts app.
  2. Create a new contact or edit an existing one.
  3. Enter the main phone number.
  4. Tap the +*# button in the bottom left of the dialing pad.
  5. Tap Pause (this inserts a comma).
  6. Type the extension number after the comma. For example: 18001234567,204.
  7. Tap the checkmark to save.

Now, when you call this contact, your iPhone will automatically dial the extension after a short delay. Pause works best as the system answers quickly.

Method 3: Use “Wait” for Interactive Voice Menus (IVR Systems)

Some systems make you:

  • Press 1 for language
  • Press 2 for support
  • Then enter an extension

In these cases, timing is unpredictable. That’s where Wait helps. It makes your iPhone stop after dialing the main number and waits for you to tap a button before sending the extension. It’s represented by a semicolon (;).

Steps to add Wait:

  1. Open Contacts and edit or create a contact.
  2. Type in the main number.
  3. Tap the +*# button.
  4. Select Wait (adds a semicolon).
  5. Enter the extension. For example: 18001234567;204.
  6. Tap the checkmark to save the contact.

After the main number connects, your iPhone will show a message like “Dial 204?” Tap Yes, and it sends the extension. This method is best for customer care IVR systems, multi-step menu options, and when you’re not sure about timing.

What is the Difference Between Pause and Wait on iPhone?

Here’s the easy comparison:

If Pause doesn’t work properly, try using Wait instead.

How to Add Multiple Pauses or Waits

You can combine extensions for more complex systems. Each comma adds a short delay. For example: 18001234567,1,2;204.

This means:

  • Call the main number
  • Wait → press 1
  • Wait → press 2
  • Then ask before dialing extension 204

This is useful for companies where you must go through menu options before reaching the extension.

How to Dial an Extension Automatically on iPhone

If you want the extension to dial without you doing anything, use Pause.

While entering a number in Contacts:

  1. Press +*#.
  2. Choose Pause.
  3. Add the extension.

Alternative shortcut:

  • Press and hold* to insert a comma (Pause).
  • Press and hold # to insert a semicolon (Wait).

Then save the contact. From now on, dialing that contact will automatically include the extension.

Troubleshooting: Phone Extension Not Working on iPhone?

If your extension isn’t working, here are common fixes.

Final Thoughts

Dialing an extension on an iPhone is easy once you know the difference between manual dialing, Pause, and wait.

  • Manual entry for one-time calls.
  • Pause (,) for automatic extensions.
  • Wait (;) when timing matters.

Save frequent numbers with extensions in your contacts, and you’ll never struggle with office phone systems again.

If you found this guide helpful, consider bookmarking it or sharing it with someone who always struggles with automated phone menus.

  • iPhone call failed? What does it mean and how to fix it?
  • How to recover deleted call history on iPhone
  • How to use T9 dialing on an iPhone

title.rendered: AirTag 2 vs AirTag 1: Key Differences Explained

content.rendered:
Apple’s AirTag quickly became one of the most popular Bluetooth trackers when it launched in 2021. Designed to help you find misplaced items, like keys, wallets, or bags, it works seamlessly with the Apple Find My network to pinpoint lost belongings.

After nearly five years without a major update, Apple has finally released the AirTag 2. It focused on smarter tracking, better range, louder sound, and improved connectivity while keeping the things that already worked great.

In this article, we’ll compare AirTag 2 vs AirTag and explain what’s new, what stayed the same, and whether the upgrade is worth it.

Table of Contents
  • AirTag 2 vs. AirTag: Quick Specs Comparison
  • Difference Between AirTag 2 and AirTag 1
    • Design and Build
    • Core Tracking Technology
    • Battery and Power
    • Chipset and Performance
    • Security and Privacy Enhancements
    • Software and Ecosystem Features
    • AirTag 2 vs AirTag: Price & Value
  • Should You Upgrade to AirTag 2?
  • Final Verdict: Which AirTag Should You Buy

AirTag 2 vs. AirTag: Quick Specs Comparison

Difference Between AirTag 2 and AirTag 1

Now, let’s go into a detailed comparison and understand the upgrades in AirTag 2.

Design and Build

While AirTag 2 brings technical upgrades, the overall look remains nearly identical to the original: the same white, circular tag that fits in standard accessories. Therefore, it fits all existing accessories; there is no need to buy new cases or holders.

Apple has used 85% recycled plastic in the AirTag Gen 2’s enclosure and 100% fiber-based packaging. It also continues to offer IP67 water and dust-resistance, meaning the tracker can handle rain or splashes in puddles.

However, the newest model is just slightly heavier, largely due to internal upgrades.

Core Tracking Technology

AirTag 2 uses a newer second-generation U2 chip, which is seen in 2025’s iPhone and Apple Watch lineup. It enhances directional tracking and extends Precision Finding’s effective range by up to ~50%. You can also use the latest Apple Watch to pinpoint your AirTag.

Moreover, the updated Bluetooth chip in AirTag 2 works seamlessly with the global Find My network and improves how far away your device can be detected. So, far-off tracking is now more reliable.

In everyday use, this means you can locate nearby items from greater distances and receive smoother haptic, visual, and audio-guided feedback through iPhone or Apple Watch.

Battery and Power

Both generations use the replaceable CR2032 coin cell battery with roughly similar capacity. Apple still cites the same “more than a year” battery life per AirTag, depending on usage.

However, now you need to wait at least 5 seconds between removing and reinserting the battery when resetting your AirTag 2.

Chipset and Performance

The U2 Ultra-Wideband chip in AirTag 2 delivers better tracking response. Users should also notice more reliable connections and slightly faster tracking startup times, thanks to the improved internals.

You can also hear your AirTag’s chime from a long distance thanks to 50% louder speakers. On the other hand, internal teardowns suggest optimized board and component design, which may also help achieve better efficiency over the long run.

Security and Privacy Enhancements

Apple has maintained and strengthened protections against unwanted tracking. If an unknown AirTag travels with you, your iPhone sends tracking notifications, just like with the first-gen.

All Find My communications also remain end-to-end encrypted, preserving privacy. In the 2nd gen, Apple has secured the speaker magnets more firmly to prevent physical tampering.

Software and Ecosystem Features

AirTag 2 requires iOS 26 or later for better support for sharing and tracking features. The Find My app still powers item location, but improved Precision Finding and Apple Watch integration make it easier to use.

Additionally, AirTag 2 supports expanded Share Item Location options, letting you share location temporarily with partners like airlines for baggage assistance.

Apple continues to update both generations, though AirTag 2 may receive longer-term support thanks to its newer hardware.

AirTag 2 vs AirTag: Price & Value

Both versions are priced at $29 per unit. Four-pack bundles are also still available for approximately $99.

So, considering the upgrades, especially better range, louder sound, and Apple Watch integration, the value improves, especially if tracking precision matters to you.

Should You Upgrade to AirTag 2?

If you rely on AirTags to track important items or want the best possible range and findability, especially with Apple Watch support, the upgrade is worth considering. For casual users, the original remains useful and may be found discounted.

On the other hand, AirTag 2 is the obvious choice for first-time buyers. All improvements come at the same price as before.

Final Verdict: Which AirTag Should You Buy

In the Apple AirTag 2 vs AirTag comparison, the 2026 model is better at:

  • Longer Precision Finding range and stronger Bluetooth detection.
  • A louder speaker for easier locating.
  • Apple Watch support makes searching more convenient.
  • Slight internal performance upgrades and improved privacy.

What hasn’t improved

  • Battery type & life are essentially the same.
  • Physical design hasn’t changed.
  • Still no GPS; reliant on Find My network.

Therefore, if you want the best Apple tracking experience, go for AirTag 2. However, if you’re happy with basic tracking or find a great deal on the original AirTag, it’s still a very capable tracker.

title.rendered: How to Use Cinematic Mode on iPhone: A Beginner’s Guide

content.rendered:
Creating professional-looking videos on an iPhone can feel limiting. Standard video keeps everything in focus, which often makes clips look flat and less engaging. Achieving cinematic background blur typically requires expensive cameras or complex editing software. That’s exactly where Apple’s Cinematic mode comes in.

Introduced with iPhone 13, Cinematic mode adds shallow depth of field, smart focus shifts, and lets you edit focus even after recording. All of it works right inside the Camera app. With just a few taps, you can turn everyday videos into polished, movie-style clips without any advanced skills.

Here’s everything you need to know about the Cinematic mode on iPhone.

Table of Contents
  • What is Cinematic Mode on iPhone?
  • What is the Difference Between Cinematic and Normal Video on iPhone?
  • Which iPhones Have Cinematic Mode?
  • How to Record a Cinematic Video with Your iPhone Camera
  • How to Edit a Cinematic Video on iPhone
  • Tips to shoot better cinematic videos on iPhone
  • Common Cinematic Mode Problems and Fixes
  • Signing Off…

What is Cinematic Mode on iPhone?

Cinematic mode is a video recording mode on iPhones that adds a beautiful depth-of-field effect to your videos, which is to say, it blurs the background to emphasize focus on the subject. This effect gives the video a professional appeal, which many refer to as “movie-like aesthetics.”

iPhones use computational photography combining software and hardware capabilities to mimic the behavior of professional cameras. Put simply, Cinematic mode captures high-quality depth data in Dolby Vision HDR at 30 frames per second to determine the exact distance between the camera and all the subjects in the frame. Then, combined with machine learning from the Neural Engine, the camera smartly picks what to focus on and when to apply focus transitions. You can manually lock focus on a subject, like a person or a thing, to track them throughout the scene if needed.

Another standout feature of Cinematic mode is that it enables your iPhone camera to adjust focus dynamically. For example, if a new subject comes into the frame or the current one looks away, the focus changes automatically. This guides the viewers’ attention and helps tell a story better. Moreover, you can even change the focus or tweak the bokeh effect after the video has been shot.

What is the Difference Between Cinematic and Normal Video on iPhone?

If you’re wondering how a Cinematic mode video differs from a standard video, here’s what you need to do.

  • Focus control: With Cinematic mode, you can manually or automatically shift focus between subjects. In a normal video, though, focus stays fixed or changes only on touch.
  • Depth-of-field effect: Cinematic mode offers a blurred background effect, while normal video captures all elements in focus.
  • Frame rate: Cinematic mode records at 30fps for a cinematic aesthetic, whereas normal video supports a variety of frame rates and resolutions.
  • Editing options: You can edit the depth-of-field effect and focus points on Cinematic mode videos after recording. However, such adjustments are unavailable in standard video.

These differences significantly improve the iPhone’s capabilities as a filmmaking device and create exciting new possibilities for video production, particularly on a low budget or with limited resources.

Tip

If you want more manual controls for capturing videos, you can use Final Cut Camera on your iPhone. It lets you adjust most of the video settings, track real-time audio levels, and supports live previews and multi-cam recordings.

Which iPhones Have Cinematic Mode?

Cinematic mode is available on the following iPhone models:

  • iPhone 13, 13 mini, 13 Pro, and 13 Pro Max
  • iPhone 14, 14 Plus, 14 Pro, and 14 Pro Max
  • iPhone 15, 15 Plus, 15 Pro, and 15 Pro Max
  • iPhone 16, 16 Plus, 16 Pro, and 16 Pro Max
  • iPhone 17, 17 Pro, and 17 Pro Max

These devices feature advanced A-series chips and enhanced camera hardware to support Cinematic mode.

How to Record a Cinematic Video with Your iPhone Camera

Now that you understand the feature well, let’s learn how to use Cinematic mode on an iPhone to elevate your video content, whether you’re a beginner or a budding filmmaker.

Recording a cinematic video is straightforward. This is what the process looks like:

  1. Open the Camera app on your iPhone.
  2. Swipe to Cinematic mode and set the frame.
  3. Tap the Cinematic mode button to reveal controls for focal length, flash, and exposure.
  4. Next, tap the f (Aperture) button, then adjust the depth using the slider that appears to add or remove background blur.
  5. Similarly, you can adjust the Exposure or turn the Flash on or off.
  6. On iPhone 16 models, you can use the Camera Control button to adjust focus depth, exposure, and zoom.
  7. Tap on a person or object in the frame to lock focus.
  8. Tap the Record button to start recording.

By default, Cinematic mode records in 1080p at 30 fps. However, you can also change the recording quality before starting the video by tapping the resolution and frame rate options at the top right of the Camera app, then switch to 4K for better clarity and choose between 24 or 30 fps on iPhone 14 and later models.

How to Edit a Cinematic Video on iPhone

Editing Cinematic mode videos is easy and doesn’t require additional tools. You can adjust focus and blurring level even after capturing the video. Here’s how:

  1. Go to the Photos app and open the cinematic video you just shot.
  2. Tap the Edit icon from the bottom toolbar.
  3. Scrub through the timeline to select the frame you want to edit.
  4. Tap on any subject to change focus at that moment.
  5. Tap the f button, then use the slider to adjust blur strength.
  6. You can also manually delete focus transitions by tapping the focus dots on the timeline.
  7. Tap Done to save the changes.

You can also apply a filter, trim the clip, adjust color, etc., just like normal videos. For a detailed guide, check out how to edit videos on iPhone and iPad.

Tips to shoot better cinematic videos on iPhone

Here are some tips to make the most of Cinematic mode:

  • Lighting should be appropriate: The subject should be well-lit. Cinematic mode performs best in good lighting conditions. Low light can reduce the effectiveness of the depth-of-field effect. Consider using portable lights for indoor or nighttime shoot positions for consistent lighting.
  • Stabilize your iPhone: Shaky footage can detract from the cinematic look. Use an iPhone tripod or stabilizer to keep your shots smooth and professional.
  • Experiment with angles: Try different angles and perspectives to make your videos more engaging.
  • Keep subjects at a suitable distance: For the best depth-of-field effect, ensure there is adequate distance between your subject and the background.
  • Use accessories: Step up your game with videography accessories like external microphones and attachable lenses, which add a more cinematic look to whatever you’re filming.

Common Cinematic Mode Problems and Fixes

Signing Off…

The Cinematic mode on iPhones is a game-changer if you want to shoot professional-quality videos without expensive equipment. With its advanced features and editing capabilities, you can easily produce visually stunning content right on your iPhone.

So go ahead and try the mode yourself. With a little practice, you should soon be able to shoot cinematic videos with your iPhone like a pro.

FAQs

What is the difference between the Action mode and the Cinematic mode?

Action mode is designed for stabilization during fast movements, while Cinematic mode focuses on adding depth-of-field effects and dynamic focus transitions. To learn more, go through our guide on using Action mode on iPhones.

Can I use Cinematic mode with the front-facing camera?

Yes, Cinematic mode works with the front-facing camera on supported iPhones.

What resolution can I record in Cinematic mode?

You can record in up to 4k resolution at 24, 25, or 30 fps on iPhone 14 and later models or 1080p at 30fps on iPhone 13 series.

Can I turn off Cinematic mode after recording?

No, but you can edit the video to reduce the depth-of-field effect. Open the video in the Photos app, tap the edit icon, select the f button, and move the slider all the way to the right.

mainEntity.name: Do I need third-party apps to edit PDFs on Mac?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between the Action mode and the Cinematic mode?

acceptedAnswer.text: Action mode is designed for stabilization during fast movements, while Cinematic mode focuses on adding depth-of-field effects and dynamic focus transitions. To learn more, go through our guide on using Action mode on iPhones.

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, Cinematic mode works with the front-facing camera on supported iPhones.

mainEntity.name: What resolution can I record in Cinematic mode?

acceptedAnswer.text: You can record in up to 4k resolution at 24, 25, or 30 fps on iPhone 14 and later models or 1080p at 30fps on iPhone 13 series.

acceptedAnswer.text: No, but you can edit the video to reduce the depth-of-field effect. Open the video in the Photos app, tap the edit icon, select the f button, and move the slider all the way to the right.

blockGraphs.question: What is the difference between the Action mode and the Cinematic mode?
blockGraphs.answer: Action mode is designed for stabilization during fast movements, while Cinematic mode focuses on adding depth-of-field effects and dynamic focus transitions. To learn more, go through our guide on using Action mode on iPhones.

blockGraphs.question: Can I use Cinematic mode with the front-facing camera?
blockGraphs.answer: Yes, Cinematic mode works with the front-facing camera on supported iPhones.

blockGraphs.question: What resolution can I record in Cinematic mode?
blockGraphs.answer: You can record in up to 4k resolution at 24, 25, or 30 fps on iPhone 14 and later models or 1080p at 30fps on iPhone 13 series.

blockGraphs.question: Can I turn off Cinematic mode after recording?
blockGraphs.answer: No, but you can edit the video to reduce the depth-of-field effect. Open the video in the Photos app, tap the edit icon, select the f button, and move the slider all the way to the right.

title.rendered: Apple Downplays Impact of Rising RAM and SSD Prices on Profit Margins

content.rendered:
Apple CEO Tim Cook has addressed concerns around rising RAM and SSD storage chip prices, assuring investors that the impact on the company’s finances remains limited for now.

Speaking during Apple’s latest earnings call with equity analysts, Cook said higher memory component costs had only a “minimal impact” on Apple’s gross margin in the fourth quarter of 2025. However, he acknowledged that the company expects “a bit more of an impact” in the current quarter.

Cook added that Apple is closely tracking the situation and will consider “a range of options” over the long term if supply chain pricing pressures continue

Strong Earnings Despite Supply Chain Pressure

Despite rising memory component costs, Apple delivered a standout quarter. The company reported record revenue of $143.8 billion, up 16 percent year over year.

Looking ahead, Apple is forecasting continued momentum, projecting revenue growth between 13 percent and 16 percent year over year in the current quarter. The company also expects its gross margin to land between 48 percent and 49 percent, underscoring the resilience of its business even as component prices climb.

What This Means Going Forward

While memory chip prices are clearly trending upward across the industry, Apple’s scale and long-term supplier relationships appear to be cushioning the immediate impact. Cook’s comments suggest the company is prepared to adapt if cost pressures persist, though no specific measures were outlined.

For now, Apple’s strong margins and revenue growth indicate that higher RAM and SSD prices are not derailing its financial performance.

iGeeksBlog Take

Apple’s massive scale and tight control over its supply chain continue to pay off. Even as memory prices rise, strong margins show Apple still has room to absorb costs, at least in the short term. The bigger question is how long this cushion lasts if chip prices keep climbing.

What do you think about Apple’s ability to absorb rising component costs? Share your thoughts in the comments.

title.rendered: Apple Reports Its Biggest Quarter Ever as Revenue Reaches $143.7 Billion

content.rendered:
Apple has delivered the strongest quarter in its history, reporting record results for fiscal Q1 2026 and comfortably exceeding market expectations. The performance underscores the company’s continued reliance on iPhone demand and its steadily expanding Services business.

For the quarter ended December 27, 2025, Apple posted total revenue of $143.7 billion, up 16% year over year. Net profit reached $42.09 billion, while earnings per share rose to $2.84, marking an all-time high for the company.

iPhone and Services Drive Growth

iPhone remained Apple’s primary revenue engine, generating $85.27 billion during the quarter. Strong demand across global markets made it the best iPhone quarter Apple has ever reported, reinforcing the product’s central role in the company’s business.

Apple’s Services segment also delivered record results, producing $30.01 billion in revenue and growing at a double-digit rate compared to last year. With more than 2.5 billion active devices now in use worldwide, Apple continues to benefit from a large installed base that supports recurring revenue through digital services and subscriptions.

Other hardware categories provided steady contributions. Mac revenue totaled $8.39 billion, while iPad brought in $8.50 billion. The Wearables, Home, and Accessories segment added $11.49 billion, reflecting consistent demand across Apple’s broader product ecosystem.

Also read: Apple Reaches $4 Trillion Milestone, Joining Microsoft and Nvidia

Strong Cash Flow and Shareholder Returns

Apple generated nearly $54 billion in operating cash flow during the quarter, supported by strong margins and disciplined cost control. The company returned close to $32 billion to shareholders, continuing its long-standing approach to capital returns.

Earnings per share increased 19% from a year earlier, highlighting Apple’s ability to translate revenue growth into higher profitability.

Momentum Heading Into 2026

The record-setting quarter confirms Apple’s optimistic outlook entering the December period and sets a high benchmark for the rest of fiscal 2026. While the broader tech industry continues to face uneven demand, Apple’s latest results point to a business entering the new year with strong momentum, loyal customers, and a financial model that continues to scale.
