title.rendered: Apple’s Foldable iPhone May Look More Like an iPad Than a Phone

content.rendered:
Apple is reportedly lining up a foldable iPhone for release next year, and a new mockup offers a hint of what could set it apart in a crowded market. While foldable phones aren’t new, this model suggests Apple is taking a distinctive approach, diverging from the competition.

A user named Subsy crafted the model, shared online, using leaked CAD files allegedly connected to Apple’s production plans. Though not exact, details like the hinge aren’t Apple’s, this mockup allows a peek into the possible future. It’s a glimpse at where Apple’s design priorities might be aimed.

Apple Seems Focused on the Unfolded Experience

The design of this foldable device echoes an iPad mini more than a typical smartphone when opened. This alone differentiates it. Instead of making a phone taller, Apple appears to be focusing on a broader display that remains practical when unfolded.

This design choice has an inherent trade-off. Once closed, the device becomes more box-like compared to Apple’s existing handsets. Most other foldables aim for a tall, slender profile when shut, aligning with users’ habitual grip. Yet, Apple seems ready to break with that norm for the sake of a larger internal screen.

A broader aspect ratio implies that the unfolded display isn’t just about size. Apple might be aiming for functionality, something conducive to reading or multitasking, rather than merely a bigger phone screen.

Also Read: iPhone Fold Could Dominate 22% of Foldable Market in Debut Year

Software May Hint at What’s Coming Next

Even if Apple holds back any formal announcement about a foldable iPhone, their software updates could offer clues. During their developer conference in June, Apple might introduce new ways for apps to adapt to these unconventional screen sizes, quietly laying the groundwork for developers.

Apple has deployed similar strategies before, prepping developers well before unveiling major hardware innovations. If repeated, these updates could suggest that a foldable iPhone is nearing reality.

While nothing is set in stone, this model aligns with a familiar Apple strategy. Entering late, ignoring trends, and creating something they believe improves on existing norms. If accurate, Apple’s foldable iPhone could redefine the category, not solely because of its folding ability, but through its reimagined concept of a foldable device.

Would a foldable iPhone appeal to you? Share your thoughts below.

acceptedAnswer.text: Apple’s official engraving service does not affect your AirPods warranty or AppleCare coverage. mainEntity.name: Are virus removal apps safe?

acceptedAnswer.text: They’re not needed for calendar spam and won’t offer any extra protection. Built-in iPhone security already handles this issue.

mainEntity.name: Can I use text effects when messaging Android users?

acceptedAnswer.text: Text effects only work with iMessage. Messages sent to Android phones appear as plain text.

mainEntity.name: Do text effects work on Mac?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, the Messages app on macOS supports text effects on compatible macOS versions, though the interface differs slightly.

mainEntity.name: Can I animate emojis using text effects?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, emojis can be selected and animated just like text, which often appears subtler than large emoji reactions.

mainEntity.name: Best filters for a clean, minimal feed?

acceptedAnswer.text: A clean, minimal feed benefits from filters that make subtle adjustments rather than visible changes. Filters that gently lift brightness, control contrast, and avoid strong color casts usually work best.

mainEntity.name: How to find trending effects?

acceptedAnswer.text: Trending effects often appear repeatedly in popular Reels. Tapping the effect name shown above a Reel lets you preview and save it. The Effects gallery in the Stories camera also highlights trending options, although these rotate frequently.

mainEntity.name: Can too many effects hurt engagement?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Overusing effects can distract viewers and make content feel cluttered or inconsistent. Effects are most effective when they support the story or mood rather than compete with it.

mainEntity.name: Are filters and effects free?

acceptedAnswer.text: Instagram’s built-in filters and most AR effects are free. While some third-party apps sell presets or editing tools, Instagram itself does not charge for filters or effects.

title.rendered: iPhone Not Receiving Texts from Android: Causes and Fixes

content.rendered:
Missing text messages from Android users is one of those problems that feels outdated but still affects a surprising number of iPhone users. You might notice Android friends saying they replied or group chats going silent. In most cases, the issue has little to do with the Android phone itself and everything to do with how iMessage, SMS, RCS, and carrier networks interact behind the scenes.

This post details why Android texts fail to reach an iPhone and provides reliable fixes, starting with quick checks and moving to advanced solutions only when needed.

Table of Contents
  • Why iPhone Is Not Receiving Text Messages From Android
  • How to Fix iPhone Not Receiving Texts From Android
    • 1. Turn Airplane Mode Off and On to Refresh Network Connection
    • 2. Check MMS and Group Messaging Settings on iPhone
    • 3. Make Sure the Android Sender Is Not Blocked
    • 4. Delete Old Messages to Free Up Storage and Fix Sync Issues
    • 5. Update iOS to Fix Message Delivery Bugs
    • 6. Update Carrier Settings on iPhone
    • 7. Reset Network Settings to Fix SMS and MMS Issues
    • 8. Reset All iPhone Settings Without Deleting Data
    • 9. Turn Off RCS Chat Features on the Android Phone
    • 10. Contact Your Mobile Carrier for SMS Troubleshooting
  • Signing Off..

Why iPhone Is Not Receiving Text Messages From Android

Before fixing the issue, it helps to understand what usually causes it.

  • iMessage interference: If your phone number is incorrectly registered with iMessage, Android messages may never switch to SMS delivery. This is common after switching phones or restoring backups.
  • RCS and SMS mismatch: Most Android phones now default to RCS. When RCS cannot properly fall back to SMS for an iPhone recipient, messages may appear sent on Android but never arrive.
  • Carrier or SIM-level problems: SMS is controlled by your mobile carrier. If SMS routing is blocked, misconfigured, or temporarily down, Android texts will not arrive.
  • Incorrect iPhone settings: Blocked contacts, incorrect default SIM selection, or date and time issues can silently stop messages.
  • Group messaging limitations: Mixed Android and iPhone group chats still rely on MMS. If MMS provisioning fails on your line, group messages will stop appearing.

How to Fix iPhone Not Receiving Texts From Android

Before changing deeper settings, rule out the basics:

  • Restart your iPhone and ask the Android sender to restart their phone.
  • Make sure you have a cellular signal, as SMS does not work over Wi-Fi alone.
  • Confirm that the date and time are set to Automatic in iPhone settings.

Once you have checked the above, you can proceed with the following fixes.

1. Turn Airplane Mode Off and On to Refresh Network Connection

If your iPhone is not receiving text messages from an Android smartphone, refreshing your network connection is a good option. This is the simplest and most reliable method because text messages are delivered over cellular networks rather than Wi-Fi.

  1. Scroll down from the right of your screen to invoke Control Center.
    On iPhones with a Home Button, you need to swipe up.
  2. Select the Airplane icon to turn on Airplane Mode.
  3. Tap the Airplane icon again to turn off Airplane Mode.

Wait for a few seconds, and voila, you’ll have successfully refreshed your cellular networks.

2. Check MMS and Group Messaging Settings on iPhone

If Android messages arrive normally in one-on-one conversations but fail in group chats, the issue is almost always tied to MMS provisioning on your mobile line. With iOS 26, Apple removed the visible MMS and Group Messaging controls from the Messages settings, so this behavior can no longer be corrected on the iPhone.

The only reliable fix is to contact your carrier and confirm that MMS and mixed device group messaging are enabled and correctly provisioned for your SIM or eSIM.

3. Make Sure the Android Sender Is Not Blocked

Another reason you may not be receiving texts on your Android device is that the number has been blocked on your device. You might have blocked your friends or family members due to an old feud and then forgotten about it. To unblock numbers, go to Settings → Phone app → Blocked Contacts. Here, you can see the numbers that you have blocked.

4. Delete Old Messages to Free Up Storage and Fix Sync Issues

One of the most common reasons your iPhone isn’t receiving Android messages is that your messaging inbox is full. As a result, this may be preventing you from receiving communications, particularly MMS messages, from your Android contacts. Please refer to our article to remove old messages from your iPhone.

Note: iPhone-to-iPhone messaging uses the iMessage platform, so there won’t be space issues.

5. Update iOS to Fix Message Delivery Bugs

The issue might be caused by an iOS bug on the device. Thankfully, Apple responds quickly to such annoyances by issuing an iOS update. All you have to do is update your iOS version to acquire the repairs and enjoy the new features.

  1. Go to Settings → General.
  2. Tap Software Update → check for updates.
  3. If available, tap Download and Install.

6. Update Carrier Settings on iPhone

The problem may be from your carrier’s end. When I first got my iPhone XR, I started getting error messages on the device. As it turned out, the issue was on the carrier side, and they had already issued an update to resolve it.

  1. Launch Settings.
  2. Tap General → About.

  3. Scroll down to Carrier. In some regions, you may see “Network”.

If you see “Update” next to Carrier, tap it and follow the on-screen instructions to update your carrier settings.

7. Reset Network Settings to Fix SMS and MMS Issues

If nothing else has worked, resetting network settings may be a viable alternative to resolve your iPhone not receiving messages from Android. It deletes all internet and networking-related data on your device.

  1. Open Settings. 
  2. Tap General.
  3. Scroll down and tap Transfer or Reset iPhone.
  4. Hit Reset → Reset Network Settings. 

  5. Provide your iPhone’s Password to complete the action.

8. Reset All iPhone Settings Without Deleting Data

If resetting network settings didn’t work, it’s time to consider an unpleasant option: Reset All Settings.

  1. Launch Settings. 
  2. Tap General.
  3. Scroll down and tap Transfer or Reset iPhone.
  4. Hit Reset → tap Reset All Settings. 

  5. Enter your Passcode to finish the action.

9. Turn Off RCS Chat Features on the Android Phone

So far, we have discussed troubleshooting methods for the iPhone. The problem could also be on the Android side.

RCS (Rich Communications Services) is Google’s version of iMessage to counter the growing popularity of the service. Google aims to deliver a close-to-iMessage experience with read receipts, typing indicators, group messages, and more.

If RCS service is enabled on the Android device, disable it in Messages Settings.

  1. Open the Messages app. 
  2. Click your avatar on the top right. 
  3. Tap Messages settings.

  4. General → Chat features → toggle Enable chat feature. 

10. Contact Your Mobile Carrier for SMS Troubleshooting

There may be times when the carrier experiences server issues on its end. If none of the steps work for you, contact your local carrier to troubleshoot the issue.

You can either connect with them on social media or call or email the carrier directly to report the issue.

Signing Off..

iPhones that are not receiving texts from Android devices are rarely a hardware problem. In most cases, it is caused by iMessage conflicts, RCS mismatches, or carrier-level SMS issues. Once the correct setting or registration is fixed, messages usually resume instantly.

If this guide helped you fix the issue, share which step worked in the comments. It may save someone else hours of frustration.

  • How to fix iMessage needs to be enabled to send this message error
  • iMessage Waiting for Activation error on iPhone?

title.rendered: New iPhone? 25 Must-Know Tips for First-Time iPhone Users (2026 Guide)

content.rendered:
So, the iPhone 17 or iPhone Air finally convinced you to switch to your first-ever iPhone, but you’re not sure where to start? Don’t worry, every iPhone user has been there. While the interface might feel different at first, Apple has designed it to be intuitive once you get the hang of it.

To help you get started and make the switch from Android to iPhone easier, here are 25 essential tips every first-time iPhone user should know.

Table of Contents
  • 1. Create an Apple Account
  • 2. Turn on Find My
  • 3. Set Up Face ID
  • 4. Customize Control Center
  • 5. Set Up Medical ID
  • 6. Use Multilingual Keyboard
  • 7. Hide or Lock Apps
  • 8. Customize the Action button
  • 9. Use Screen Time Restrictions
  • 10. Enable Sensitive Content Warning
  • 11. Take a Scrolling Screenshot
  • 12. Turn Off Your iPhone From the Control Center
  • 13. Use Safari Distraction Control
  • 14. Use the Spotlight Search
  • 15. Set Up Emergency Contact
  • 16. Enable Battery Percentage Display
  • 17. Customize Photos App
  • 18. Fully Turn Off Wi-Fi and Bluetooth
  • 19. Use Focus Mode
  • 20. Customize Lock Screen Controls
  • 21. Set Messages to Auto-Delete
  • 22. Use Family Sharing
  • 23. Scroll to the Top Instantly
  • 24. Record Calls Natively
  • 25. Try Apple Intelligence Writing Tools
  • Wrapping Up

1. Create an Apple Account

Your Apple Account (formerly Apple ID) is the key to everything in the Apple ecosystem. You’ll need it for the App Store, iCloud, iMessage, FaceTime, Find My, and more.

If you want to speed up your setup, you can even create your Apple Account beforehand using the web or your Mac.

2. Turn on Find My

Before doing anything else, enable Find My iPhone. It’s Apple’s built-in tracking tool that helps you locate your iPhone if it’s ever lost or stolen. You can make it ring, track it on a map, or remotely erase your data for security.

Want to learn more? Check out our detailed guide on using the Find My app.

3. Set Up Face ID

This is another important security measure you must undertake to safeguard your private data from unauthorized access. Face ID not only helps you unlock your iPhone but also authorizes payments and app downloads.

Once you are done setting up Face ID, you can stay at peace as no one can unlock your iPhone without you allowing them to unless they have the Passcode.

4. Customize Control Center

Simply swipe down from the top right of the display to pull down the Control Center on your iPhone. Here, you can quickly toggle Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, Mobile data, Airdrop, and more with just a tap of an in-display button.

While the default setup isn’t bad either, Apple’s iOS 18 allows you to customize the Control Center completely. You can add/remove toggles, resize them, create a new Control Center screen, or even delete one altogether.

5. Set Up Medical ID

Accidents and medical emergencies can happen anytime, so it’s important to be prepared for them in some capacity. The Medical ID on your iPhone stores all your vital information about your medical health, such as your allergies, medications, emergency contacts, and more.

Setting up the Medical ID on your iPhone in advance can help the first responder know about your health condition in an emergency.

6. Use Multilingual Keyboard

If you are well-versed in multiple languages and prefer to include words from each in a single sentence but switching keyboards while typing feels time-consuming, your iPhone can help you.

Apple, with the latest iOS 18, added multilingual keyboard support to the supported iPhones. You can add up to three different languages to your iPhone keyboard and switch between them simultaneously while typing. Any word you type in English is automatically translated to another selected language.

To set up a multilingual keyboard on your iPhone:

  1. Go to Settings → General → Keyboards → Keyboards.

  2. Tap English (your primary language) → Add Language.

7. Hide or Lock Apps

There are many apps on our iPhones that we don’t want others to have access to or even know that they exist on our iPhones. While hiding or locking apps wasn’t possible earlier, iOS 18 has bought this most requested feature as well.

To lock and hide apps on your iPhone, simply press and hold the app → tap Require Face ID → select whether you want to lock or hide the app.

8. Customize the Action button

Starting with the iPhone 15 Pro, Apple replaced the mute slider with a new Action Button. While the Action Button, by default, is programmed to do the same job the mute slider used to do, you can customize it to perform other tasks, such as turning on Focus, Flashlight, recognizing music, and more.

However, unlike other physical buttons, you must press hold the Action Button for it to function instead of simply pressing it.

To customize the Action button, head to Settings → Action Button.

9. Use Screen Time Restrictions

As the name suggests, Screen Time restrictions help you limit your screen time by managing content, apps, and settings on your iPhone. The feature is most useful when managing your child’s iPhone or if you want to control your phone usage.

Do read our detailed guide on how to use Screen Time on your iPhone.

10. Enable Sensitive Content Warning

The internet is a dangerous place, so protecting yourself from exposure to inappropriate online content is paramount. While you can decide not to visit such websites, you can do anything if someone sends you something inappropriate via FaceTime, Messages, AirDrop, and other apps. This is exactly where Sensitive Content Warning comes in.

Once enabled, the Sensitive Content Warning blurs any image it deems sensitive and inappropriate received via the said apps and will display a “This may be sensitive” dialog box over it.

To enable Sensitive Content Warning, go to Settings → Privacy & Security → Sensitive Content Warning.

11. Take a Scrolling Screenshot

By now, you might have figured out how to take screenshots on your iPhone, but what about scrolling screenshots? Yes, taking a scrolling screenshot on an iPhone is not as straightforward as it is on an Android. Unlike Android, you can only take scrolling screenshots of web pages, documents, PDFs, notes, or emails. While earlier you could only save them as PDF files, this changed with iOS 17, as you can now save them as regular images. Here’s how:

Take a regular screenshot, then tap the preview tile at the bottom left to reveal it. Next, tap the Full Page tab, then tap Done to save the screenshot.

12. Turn Off Your iPhone From the Control Center

Not knowing the right button combination to turn off the iPhone is among the top frustrating moments for a new iPhone user. Luckily, you don’t have to remember it anymore. With iOS 18, Apple has added the Power button in the Control Center, making things much easier for first-time iPhone owners.

You can find the Power button at the top right corner of the Control Center. All you need to do is tap and hold it, and the power slider will appear.

13. Use Safari Distraction Control

Like Chrome is for Google, Safari is Apple’s proprietary web browser, which Apple has reserved for Apple devices, including the iPhone. Like any other web browser, Safari web pages can also annoy you with unwanted elements like sign-in prompts and cookie preference popups. But unlike other browsers, Safari offers you a way to hide them and keep your web page as clean as you want.

Do read our exclusive guide on the Safari Distraction Control feature to learn more about it.

14. Use the Spotlight Search

Spotlight Search on iPhone makes it super easy to find what you’re looking for on your iPhone. It can literally help you with anything on your iPhone, be it finding events on your calendar, files, apps, TV shows, or dedicated settings option, and even name, place, or person in photos.

So, the next time you have difficulty finding anything on your iPhone, simply make a small down swipe to access the Spotlight Search.

15. Set Up Emergency Contact

Along with the Medical ID, you can also add emergency contacts on your iPhone. Just like the Medical ID, the emergency contact will let the first responder know whom to contact when you are in an emergency.

16. Enable Battery Percentage Display

One thing that even I hated when I switched to the iPhone was finding out Apple hadn’t enabled the battery percentage indicator by default, and I am sure you, too, would hate this fact. There is no way one could make out exactly how long their battery will last by simply looking at the battery indicator with no number on it.

Luckily, unlike other basic features, Apple lets you enable the battery percentage indicator via the settings. To do so, go to Settings → Battery → toggle on Battery Percentage.

17. Customize Photos App

If you had moved to the iPhone before the arrival of iOS 18, you would have been satisfied with how the Photos app used to look. However, Apple completely redesigned the Photos app in iOS 18, leaving even the seasoned user confused, let alone new iPhone users. You get a single scrollable screen instead of multiple tabs.

Thankfully, Apple allows you to customize the Photos app on your iPhone, so you can rearrange things according to your preferences. All you need to do is scroll down to the bottom of the Photos app, hit the Customize button and start customizing.

18. Fully Turn Off Wi-Fi and Bluetooth

Another weird thing about the iPhone is that even when you disable Bluetooth and Wi-Fi from the Control Center, they are not truly disabled. Both services still stay active in the background. You must disable both services within the iPhone Settings to completely turn them off.

19. Use Focus Mode

An advanced version of the Do Not Disturb mode, the Focus mode on the iPhone helps you limit distractions and concentrate on the things that matter most. You can customize the focus options to your preference, such as work, sleep, personal, fitness, and more.

Do read our detailed guide on how to use Focus on iPhone to learn more.

20. Customize Lock Screen Controls

Do you also get frustrated when the flashlight gets activated out of nowhere without you even knowing? Well, most of the time, this happens when you accidentally press the flashlight button on the Lock Screen. While there is no solution for this on Android, you can customize the lock screen on your iPhone or remove the flashlight control altogether.

21. Set Messages to Auto-Delete

There is no point in having countless older messages eating valuable space on your iPhone for no good reason. However, with tens of promotional and spam messages arriving daily, deleting each message manually isn’t feasible. To help you with that, the iPhone lets you choose a time frame for auto-deleting messages. Here’s how:

Open Settings → Apps → Messages → Keep Messages → Choose time period.

22. Use Family Sharing

Buying your first iPhone can help you save money if other family members also own Apple devices. Once set up and enabled, Family Sharing lets you share your subscriptions for Apple services, including iCloud+, Apple Music, Apple TV+, Apple Fitness+, Apple News+, and Apple Arcade, without sharing the Apple Account.

Read our dedicated guide to learn What is Apple Family Sharing and How to Use It?

23. Scroll to the Top Instantly

Do you ever find yourself scrolling so much that returning to the top of the screen takes an eternity? Well, here’s a fantastic iPhone tip that every new user should be aware of. Simply tap at the top of the screen, and you’ll automatically return to the top of whatever you’re scrolling through.

24. Record Calls Natively

After years of anticipation, Apple finally added native call recording support to iPhones with iOS 18. However, the recording process isn’t discreet; the iPhone lets the person know the call will be recorded when you hit the record button.

Do read our detailed guide on call recording on iPhone to learn more.

25. Try Apple Intelligence Writing Tools

Although a bit late, Apple also joined the AI bandwagon with iOS 18. Writing tools are among the various features of Apple Intelligence, which you can use to proofread and rewrite text directly on your iPhone. This eliminates the need to pay for paid tools such as Grammarly. However, in order to experience this feature, you must own an Apple Intelligence-supported iPhone, i.e., iPhone 15 Pro or later models.

Wrapping Up

Your new iPhone can do much more than you might expect at first glance. These tips will help you navigate iOS confidently and discover what makes Apple’s ecosystem so seamless.

Explore, experiment, and enjoy your new iPhone. If you’ve found a hidden gem or clever trick, share it in the comments to help other first-time users.

Also read:

  • iPhone settings you should change
  • 25+ Hidden iPhone and iPad Keyboard Tips to Type Smarter
  • Tips to make iPhone safe and secure

title.rendered: WhatsApp Is Testing a New Peripheral Section in Linked Devices on iOS

content.rendered:
WhatsApp is introducing a new feature to improve user experience: a dedicated Peripherals section in the Linked Devices area. According to WABetaInfo, the new section lists devices that automatically connect to a WhatsApp account in the background, without requiring a QR code scan or a six-digit verification code.

Peripheral devices differ from connected ones as they require no manual pairing. These are designed to link silently once the necessary app is installed and account criteria are met, facilitating a quick, user-free connection. This functionality suits accessories and wearables that depend on smooth syncing.

Table of Contents
  • Apple Watch Is Currently the Only Supported Peripheral
  • No Manual Disconnect Option Inside WhatsApp
  • Improved Transparency and Account Awareness
  • Gradual Rollout Beyond Beta Users

Apple Watch Is Currently the Only Supported Peripheral

Currently, WhatsApp supports only the Apple Watch as a peripheral device. Once the app is installed on the watch and is part of Apple’s connected ecosystem, it will autonomously form a connection with WhatsApp. This results in the Apple Watch appearing as its own entry under Linked Devices, joining other linked clients like Macs.

Each peripheral entry displays details like the device’s name and its last active time, mirroring the format used for other linked devices and ensuring all connected hardware remains visible.

No Manual Disconnect Option Inside WhatsApp

Unlike other linked devices, users can’t remove a peripheral device directly via WhatsApp settings. To sever the link, the corresponding app must be uninstalled from the device. For instance, taking WhatsApp off an Apple Watch stops message syncing and removes it from the linked devices list.

While this adds an extra step, it guarantees that the device won’t inadvertently sync messages, maintaining user control over their connections.

Improved Transparency and Account Awareness

Integrating peripherals alongside conventional linked devices gives users a clearer picture of which hardware accesses their account. This could cut down confusion related to notification and message delivery, vital for users juggling multiple devices.

Additionally, it boosts security awareness. Seeing an Apple Watch listed that a user doesn’t own could signal unauthorized access through their Apple ID. Users can then evaluate their account’s security and devices.

Gradual Rollout Beyond Beta Users

While initially visible only to those using the iOS beta via TestFlight, some on the App Store version of WhatsApp are beginning to see this feature. This indicates the rollout isn’t just for beta users.

When widely available, the peripheral view should give users better visibility into how WhatsApp works with wearables and similar devices.

Have you noticed the new peripherals feature in WhatsApp on your iOS device? Let us know in the comments, especially if the Apple Watch integration is appearing for you.

title.rendered: Apple May Be Testing the iPhone 18 Earlier Than Ever

content.rendered:
Apple is seemingly accelerating its timeline for the upcoming iPhone 18 model. Reports indicate the company is already moving into the early stages of testing production for what is expected to be the iPhone 18. Should these reports hold true, Apple would be embarking on one of its earliest production starts for a future iPhone version.

Table of Contents
  • Why Apple Is Starting So Early
  • A Clue About Apple’s Future iPhone Plans
  • Better Control Over Production and Supply
  • What This Could Mean for iPhone Fans

Why Apple Is Starting So Early

The tech giant appears to be kicking off its trial production sooner than in previous years, according to the well-informed analyst Ming-Chi Kuo. Apple is rumored to commence this preliminary phase as early as January, a notable deviation from its traditional schedule.

This early start gives Apple a chance to evaluate if its manufacturing processes are poised for efficiency. This testing phase is crucial for ensuring that, when mass production commences, the phone rolls out smoothly and is ready for global distribution without hitches.

A Clue About Apple’s Future iPhone Plans

The advance testing could hint at a broader strategy shift in Apple’s iPhone release timelines. There is some buzz around the company potentially adopting a dual-launch strategy by 2026. This happens right after strong iPhone 17 demand and shipment forecasts.

Under this plan, high-end Pro models would debut in the fall, with the entry-level and more affordable versions launching in the spring. Kicking off iPhone 18 testing this far in advance could aid Apple in gearing up for such a potentially divided launch timetable.

Better Control Over Production and Supply

Pushing testing forwards might also double as a tactical move for better management. Initiating the process earlier allows Apple to gain more command over component supplies, especially critical ones like memory. Additionally, this head start enables the company to refine its manufacturing and logistics workflow long before the public gets a peek at the new device.

Though Apple hasn’t confirmed any of these details, the proposed timeline suggests a mix of caution and enhanced strategy on their part.

What This Could Mean for iPhone Fans

For those eagerly watching the iPhone landscape, if these reports pan out, Apple is positioning itself for more seamless product releases in the future. This early commencement does not necessarily herald an expedited launch of the iPhone 18, but it certainly underscores Apple’s forward-thinking stance.

While all this remains largely behind the scenes for now, it offers a fascinating look into how Apple may be planning to reshape its iPhone release cycle in the upcoming years.

Do you think a two-phase launch strategy would impact your interest in new iPhones? Share your thoughts with us below.

title.rendered: ChatGPT Wraps Up 2025 With a Personalized Year‑in‑Review Experience

content.rendered:
OpenAI is ending 2025 with a feature many users already know and enjoy from other platforms: a personalized year‑end recap. The new experience, called Your Year with ChatGPT, gives people a snapshot of how they used the AI throughout the year, turning everyday conversations into a shareable story, something similar to Spotify Wrapped.

The feature reflects a growing trend among tech companies to make data feel more personal and engaging, rather than hidden behind charts and settings pages.

A Look Back at How You Used ChatGPT in 2025

Your Year with ChatGPT breaks down a user’s activity over the past year in a simple, visual format. It highlights key themes from conversations and includes usage stats such as how often you chatted, when you were most active, and how your interaction patterns changed over time.

Instead of focusing only on numbers, OpenAI adds personality to the recap. Each user receives a description of their chat style based on how they write or speak, along with an archetype that reflects what they mainly use ChatGPT for.

More Than Stats: Creative Touches and Future Hints

The recap goes beyond analytics by adding creative elements. Users receive a short poem inspired by their year, a personalized pixel‑style artwork, and a playful award that summarizes their overall ChatGPT journey in 2025.

OpenAI also includes light predictions for 2026, framing the feature as both a reflection on the past and a look ahead. These additions make the experience feel closer to a story than a report.

How to See Your Year With ChatGPT

Accessing the feature is simple. Follow these steps to view your year‑end recap:

  1. Open the ChatGPT app or visit ChatGPT on the web and make sure you’re signed in.
  2. Look for the Your Year with ChatGPT prompt on the home screen, or type a request like “Show me my year with ChatGPT” into the chat. Alternatively, you can also click on the Plus icon > More and see the option.
  3. Tap or submit the request to view your recap in a story‑style format that’s easy to scroll through and share.

The feature is available on both mobile and web for Free, Plus, and Pro users, as long as chat history and memory are enabled. Once you check your stats, you can proceed to ask ChatGPT questions about your year if you are interested.

Where the Feature Is Available and Who Can Use It

Your Year with ChatGPT is currently rolling out in select countries, including the United States, the United Kingdom, Canada, Australia, and New Zealand. The recap is limited to individual accounts and is not available for Education, Enterprise, or Team plans.

By introducing this feature, OpenAI is positioning ChatGPT as more than just a tool. The year‑end summary turns everyday conversations into something memorable, signaling how personal AI experiences are becoming a bigger part of modern tech platforms.

acceptedAnswer.text: Calendar viruses are caused by accidentally approving spam calendar subscriptions through deceptive websites or links.

mainEntity.name: Can calendar viruses steal my data?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Calendar spam cannot access personal data, install apps, or control your device.

mainEntity.name: Are virus removal apps safe?

acceptedAnswer.text: They’re not needed for calendar spam and won’t offer any extra protection. Built-in iPhone security already handles this issue.

mainEntity.name: Can I use text effects when messaging Android users?

acceptedAnswer.text: Text effects only work with iMessage. Messages sent to Android phones appear as plain text.

mainEntity.name: Do text effects work on Mac?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, the Messages app on macOS supports text effects on compatible macOS versions, though the interface differs slightly.

mainEntity.name: Can I animate emojis using text effects?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, emojis can be selected and animated just like text, which often appears subtler than large emoji reactions.

mainEntity.name: Best filters for a clean, minimal feed?

acceptedAnswer.text: A clean, minimal feed benefits from filters that make subtle adjustments rather than visible changes. Filters that gently lift brightness, control contrast, and avoid strong color casts usually work best.

mainEntity.name: How to find trending effects?

acceptedAnswer.text: Trending effects often appear repeatedly in popular Reels. Tapping the effect name shown above a Reel lets you preview and save it. The Effects gallery in the Stories camera also highlights trending options, although these rotate frequently.

mainEntity.name: Can too many effects hurt engagement?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Overusing effects can distract viewers and make content feel cluttered or inconsistent. Effects are most effective when they support the story or mood rather than compete with it.

mainEntity.name: Are filters and effects free?

acceptedAnswer.text: Instagram’s built-in filters and most AR effects are free. While some third-party apps sell presets or editing tools, Instagram itself does not charge for filters or effects.

title.rendered: Snapchat Quick Cut Lets You Create Music-Synced Videos in Seconds

content.rendered:
Snapchat is leaving no stone unturned to position itself as the go-to social media platform for creators. One of the biggest challenges for new creators is producing short videos that sync cleanly with a song’s beat, a process that often requires time, precision, and manual editing. Snapchat’s new Quick Cut feature directly addresses this pain point. The feature eliminates the need for manual editing and enables creators to quickly produce polished, music-synced short videos within the Snapchat app.

Read on to learn what Snapchat’s Quick Cut feature is and how to use it to make short-form video creation faster and easier.

Table of Contents
  • What Is Snapchat Quick Cut?
  • How Snapchat Quick Cut Works
  • How to Use Quick Cut on Snapchat
  • Limitations You Should Know
  • What Makes Snapchat Quick Cut a Must-Use?
  • Availability and Release Timeline
  • Start Creating With Quick Cut…

What Is Snapchat Quick Cut?

Quick Cut is a built-in short-video creation tool in the Snapchat app that automatically edits selected Memories or camera clips to match the rhythm of a song. Instead of relying on separate video editing apps or manual editing, Snapchat analyzes the selected music and aligns clip transitions precisely to the beat.

The feature positions Snapchat as a faster and more accessible alternative to traditional short-form video editors, particularly for users who want polished, music-synced videos without working with timelines, keyframes, or complex editing tools.

How Snapchat Quick Cut Works

After you select the photos and videos you want to include, Snapchat automatically applies a music track, detects beats and tempo changes, and times clip transitions accordingly. The entire edit is generated in seconds, with no manual trimming required.

You can also switch to a different song at any point. When you do, Snapchat instantly resyncs the clips to the new track, maintaining a smooth, rhythm-matched flow without any additional effort.

If a Quick Cut created by another Snapchatter inspires you, you can unlock it and replace the original media with your own photos or videos. This makes it easy to recreate trending styles while still keeping the content personal.

How to Use Quick Cut on Snapchat

Now that you know how Snapchat Quick Cut works, here’s how you can use it to create professional-looking short videos in seconds:

  1. Open the Snapchat app and swipe up on the Camera tab, or tap the Memories icon next to the camera shutter to open your Memories.
  2. Here, tap the Quick Cut banner at the top of the Memories screen.
  3. Now, select multiple photos or video clips from your Memories, Camera Roll, or a combination of both.
  4. Tap Next. Snapchat will automatically create a video and sync your clips to a default music track.
  5. Tap the music banner to choose a different song from Snapchat’s music library. Your clips will be re-synced automatically to the new track.
  6. To enhance the video, swipe through the effects carousel at the bottom and apply a visual effect. Note that changing effects may also switch the music, so reselect your preferred track if needed.
  7. Tap Next once you are satisfied with the result.
  8. Preview the final video, make any optional adjustments, then save it to Memories or share it as a Snap or Story.

Limitations You Should Know

While Quick Cut is designed for speed and simplicity, it does come with a few limitations that are worth keeping in mind before you start creating videos:

  • You cannot use your own music with Quick Cut; only tracks available in Snapchat’s built-in music library are supported.
  • Like many other Snapchat features, Quick Cut is limited to the mobile app. You cannot view or create Quick Cut videos on Snapchat Web.
  • Advanced manual editing controls are limited compared to professional editors.
  • Music selection is subject to regional availability.

What Makes Snapchat Quick Cut a Must-Use?

If you lack advanced editing skills or the time to edit videos manually, Quick Cut offers a simple way to create music-driven content. It lowers the barrier to entry by automating beat syncing, allowing casual users to produce engaging videos without editing experience, while helping creators quickly generate beat-synced clips for Stories and social sharing.

Availability and Release Timeline

Quick Cut is now available to iOS users worldwide, with Snapchat confirming that the feature will arrive on Android in the coming months. We will update this post once it does.

Start Creating With Quick Cut…

Snapchat Quick Cut is built for speed, simplicity, and visual impact. If you enjoy sharing memories set to music but dislike manual editing, this feature is worth trying. It turns everyday photos and clips into polished videos with almost no effort, directly from your phone.

If you have tried Quick Cut already, share how it fits into your content workflow.

FAQs

Can I use my own music in Quick Cut?

No. Quick Cut only supports songs available in Snapchat’s built-in music library. You cannot upload or use custom audio tracks.

Is Snapchat Quick Cut available for all devices?

Currently, Quick Cut is available on the iOS mobile app, and will soon roll out for Android and other devices. It is not supported on Snapchat Web.

aioseo_head_json.author_bio:
Vikhyat has a bachelor’s degree in Electronic and Communication Engineering and over five years of writing experience. His passion for technology and Apple products led him to the tech writing space, where he specializes in writing App features, How-to guides, and troubleshooting guides for fellow Apple users. 

 

About Vikhyat Rishi

  • Vikhyat has over five years of experience writing consumer tech content.
  • During his association with Smartprix and Beebom, Vikhyat has tested, tested, and reviewed numerous gadgets, including but not limited to smartphones, TVs, and more.
  • His passion for technology and Apple products led him to iGeeksBlog, where he specializes in writing How-to and troubleshooting guides for fellow Apple enthusiasts.

Experience

Vikhyat embarked on his journey in consumer technology writing in 2019, driven by his passion for technology. He has sharpened his skills through associations with Smartprix and Beebom, where he extensively tested and reviewed various gadgets, focusing mainly on smartphones. Currently, Vikhyat specializes in crafting How-to and troubleshooting guides for the Apple ecosystem at iGeeksBlog. When not typing away on his MacBook Air, he loves exploring the real world.

title.rendered: Best Video Editing Apps for iPhone, iPad, and Android

content.rendered:
Video has become the fastest and main way to share ideas, build brands, and grow online in 2026. From social media reels and YouTube videos to business promotions and online learning, high-quality video content is now expected across the board.

However, you no longer need a computer to edit professional videos. With the right video editing app, you can create, edit, and publish stunning videos from your smartphone. Here are the best video editing apps for iPhone, iPad, and Android, with a focus on usability, features, and real-world value for creators.

Table of Contents
  • What Makes the Best Free Video Editing App
  • 6 Best Video Editing Apps for iPhone, iPad and Android
    • 1. Adobe Premiere: Best for Content Creators
    • 2. CapCut: Shine on Social Media with AI Videos
    • 3. DaVinci Resolve for iPad: For Advanced Users
    • 4. Videoleap: AI Video Editor King
    • 5. Prequel: Enjoy Aesthetic Filters
    • 6. Afterlight: Vintage Video Editor
  • Which Video Editor Is Best for You?
  • Edit Videos On The Go!

What Makes the Best Free Video Editing App

Not all free video editing apps are worth your time. A good free app should help you create professional-looking videos and avoid nagging you to upgrade too early. Here’s what I consider before recommending:

  • Easy-to-use interface: Of course, a clean layout, drag-and-drop timeline, and clear icons are important, especially for beginners.
  • No heavy watermarks: Professional apps either do not add watermarks or barely keep them minimal.
  • Core editing tools: Trimming, splitting, transitions, text, filters, and basic color correction.
  • Export quality: HD or 4K export is a big plus, especially when targeting YouTube, Instagram, and TikTok.
  • Cross-platform availability: Apps that work on both iOS and Android give you flexibility.
  • Performance optimization: The application should run smoothly and not crash, even on long videos.

6 Best Video Editing Apps for iPhone, iPad and Android

Edit videos like a pro on your phone with these easy-to-use apps that deliver powerful tools without a learning curve.

1. Adobe Premiere: Best for Content Creators

Adobe Premiere on mobile is designed for creators looking to produce fast, clean edits with a professional feel. You can access Adobe’s creative assets library for free. If you are like me and already use Premiere Pro on a desktop, this app is a great choice. All your iPhone projects will be synced with Adobe Creative Cloud.

Key Features:

  • Multi-track timeline with studio-quality sound
  • Auto reframe for social media
  • Powerful AI-powered tools like auto captions, background expansion, etc.
  • Totally free; No ads or watermarks

Usability: Simple enough for beginners, powerful enough for semi-pro users.

Download on iPhone | Download on Android

2. CapCut: Shine on Social Media with AI Videos

CapCut is one of the most widely used free video editing apps in 2026. It’s most useful for creating short videos to be shared on social media platforms. Videos can be exported at 4K 60fps with smart HDR. You can also enjoy advanced speed curves, chroma keyframes, and stabilization.

Key Features:

  • Free trending templates, transitions, filters, and effects
  • Auto-cuts for social media
  • AI-powered story maker, translation, captions, and more
  • No watermark (in most exports)

Usability: Extremely beginner-friendly with fast results. Best for TikTok, Instagram Reels, and YouTube Shorts creators.

Download on iPhone | Download on Android

3. DaVinci Resolve for iPad: For Advanced Users

DaVinci Resolve for iPad is a professional-grade editor designed for serious creators. It uses Apple’s M-series chips to deliver desktop-level editing on a tablet. You can do Hollywood-style color grading and sync your work on Blackmagic Cloud. However, if you are a beginner and want quick editing, you may skip this.

For iPhone, you can enjoy a similar set of editing tools and features in iMovie, Apple’s official video editor.

Key Features:

  • Advanced color grading and post-production tools
  • Multi-cam editing
  • AI tools for peak creativity
  • Desktop-like timeline

Usability: Powerful enough for filmmakers and professional editors, but it has a learning curve.

Download for iPad

4. Videoleap: AI Video Editor King

Videoleap focuses on creative and AI-driven editing. You can use pre-made AI video templates or generate videos from scratch. I like its unlimited undo/redo functionality and intuitive timeline. With so many trending filters and effects, it’s perfect for eye-catching videos.

Key Features:

  • AI editing tool set and effortless background removal
  • Layer-based editing
  • Motion effects and blending
  • Text animations

Usability: Easy to begin, more advanced tools offered for creative edits, visual storytelling, and experimental videos.

Download for iPhone | Download for Android

5. Prequel: Enjoy Aesthetic Filters

Prequel focuses on style and basic video editing. It’s my favorite app when I need to share a stylish Instagram story. You get over 800 cinematic FX, filters such as Disco and Miami, and TikTok Templates. It’s great for those seeking to create fast, trendy content.

Key Features:

  • Cinematic filters
  • Aesthetic presets
  • Simple trimming tools
  • Social media-ready formats

Usability: Very easy, minimal editing complexity. Ideal for influencers, lifestyle creators, and casual users.

Download for iPhone | Download for Android

6. Afterlight: Vintage Video Editor

Afterlight focuses on mood-based edits rather than complex timelines. When creating a cinematic video, simply upload your clip and edit using 30+ vintage presets. Additionally, the authentic film overlays make your video professional and artistic. However, if you want granular editing, this isn’t the right option.

Key Features:

  • Retro filters and textures
  • Light leaks and film grain
  • Simple editing controls

Usability: Simple, focused on aesthetic video styles; not a full editor.

Download for iPhone | Download for Android

Which Video Editor Is Best for You?

Choose based on how often you edit, what platforms you publish on, and how much control you want.

Edit Videos On The Go!

By 2026, mobile video editing will no longer involve a trade-off. Instead, it will be a robust and flexible way to create professional content anytime, from anywhere. Whether you use an iPhone, iPad, or Android device, there will be a suitable video editing app for you.

If you want ease of use, choose iMovie or CapCut. If you want flexibility, try Videoleap or Prequel. For professional-grade work, DaVinci Resolve for iPad and Adobe Premiere stand out. The best app isn’t the one with the most features, it’s the one you’ll actually use consistently.

Which video editing apps have you used before? Please let us know in the comments below; I’ll try it out!

  • How to reverse a video on iPhone: Best free apps you can use

title.rendered: Best Wireless Charging Mouse Pads You Should Buy Now

content.rendered:
Wireless charging mouse pads are one of the coolest upgrades you can add to your desk. They combine a comfortable mouse mat with a built-in wireless charger, letting you power your iPhone, Android, earbuds, or other Qi-compatible devices while you work or play. These smart pads help reduce clutter, boost productivity, and make your desk look neater and tech-savvy.  

In this guide, we break down five of the best wireless charging mouse pads currently available, focusing on usability, design, charging performance, and value. 

Table of Contents
  • Who Should Get a Wireless Charging Mouse Pad?
  • 5 Best Wireless Charging Desk Mats
    • 1. GIM Wireless Charging RGB Gaming Mouse Pad – Best for Gamers
    • 2. Miroddi Magnetic Wireless Charging Desk Mat: Charge iPhone and AirPods Together
    • 3. TopMade Wireless Charging Mouse Pad: Durable & Heat-Resistant
    • 4. abc.mat Store Wireless Charging Desk Mat: Beautiful Pink Look
    • 5. HAUTOCO 3-in-1 Wireless Charging Mouse Pad: Affordable Utility
  • Wireless Charging Mouse Pad Buying Tips
    • Final Takeaway

Who Should Get a Wireless Charging Mouse Pad? 

A wireless charging desk mat is ideal for someone looking to have a clean, efficient, and modern desktop. Here’s who will like it the most: 

  • Desk workers and remote professionals: Keep your phone charging while you work, without extra cables. 
  • People with small or cluttered desks: Accommodate your keyboard, mouse, and other accessories with a charger into one space-saving mat. 
  • Gamers & creators: Enjoy RGB lighting and stay powered during long sessions without plugging in devices. 
  • Cable-free setup lovers: Reduce desk clutter and enjoy a cleaner workspace. It also protects your desk from scratches and wear. 

5 Best Wireless Charging Desk Mats

These charging desk mats keep your workspace clean while powering your phone, earbuds, and accessories in one place.

 1. GIM Wireless Charging RGB Gaming Mouse Pad – Best for Gamers

The GIM Wireless Charging Desk Mat is an excellent all-around choice. Its XL size (about 800×300 mm) and 15W fast-charging support are ideal for users who want both a large surface area and a powerful charger. 

I liked its beautiful artwork with 10 LED modes, adding a cool aesthetic touch to my setup without being too over the top. Moreover, the non-slip base keeps the pad firmly in place even during intense mouse movement. 

Best For: Gamers and multitaskers who want a stylish, functional desk mat at a good price. 

2. Miroddi Magnetic Wireless Charging Desk Mat: Charge iPhone and AirPods Together 

The Miroddi pad keeps things simple and functional. You get 15W Qi-compatible wireless charging for your Apple devices with a strong magnetic hold. The pad includes 11 RGB modes with various patterns and memory functions. 

If you have a laptop, the pad’s XXL size accommodates it and its accessories. The best part is the textured micro-weave cloth surface that’s waterproof, wear-resistant, and provides superior tracking accuracy. Plus, the one-year warranty gives peace of mind.  

Best For: Office workers or casual users who want a tough, robust desk mat with dependable charging. 

3. TopMade Wireless Charging Mouse Pad: Durable & Heat-Resistant 

If durability is your top priority, the TopMade pad focuses on long-lasting build quality and everyday usability. Its smooth-textured top surface is waterproof, easy to clean, and heat-resistant. Moreover, you can glide your mouse on it effortlessly. 

This pad also has two wireless charging areas for your phone and AirPods, supporting up to 15W magnetic wireless charging. You can see the charging status and over-temperature indication on the top light.  

Best For: People who want a smooth desk mat for both office work and light gaming. 

4. abc.mat Store Wireless Charging Desk Mat: Beautiful Pink Look 

The abc.mat Store pad gives an aesthetic upgrade to your desk. The large size has room for your keyboard, mouse, and other accessories. Additionally, the built-in magnets auto-align your phone and AirPods, and protection against overcurrent and overheating ensures secure, precise charging.  

However, it only supports a 7.5W power supply. So, if you want fast charging, you may skip this. The faux leather, high-density micro-woven fabric surface, and anti-slip rubber base make this mouse pad durable for daily use.  

Best for: Users seeking a beautiful desk mat with solid wireless charging capability. 

5. HAUTOCO 3-in-1 Wireless Charging Mouse Pad: Affordable Utility 

The HAUTOCO pad is designed to be practical and budget-friendly. It packs three magnetic wireless charging stations for your iPhone, AirPods, and Apple Watch. The best part is that you can charge your phone in a portrait or landscape position with the raised charging coil. 

Additionally, there are 15 RGB lighting modes to suit your mood. The fabric surface will allow spills and normal wear. Hence, this desk mat offers all the necessary features at an affordable price. 

Best For: Budget-minded shoppers who want powerful wireless charging and RGB lighting with their desk mat. 

Wireless Charging Mouse Pad Buying Tips 

Here are some points you should consider before making the purchase: 

  • Charging Power: Consider pads that are compatible with Qi technology and 15W power delivery. This would be sufficient for most mobile phones and other devices.  
  • Surface Feel: A smooth, low-drag surface helps your mouse move accurately. Cloth or micro-textured pads are usually comfortable and versatile.  
  • Size: Extended pads (keyboard + mouse) are great for workstations, while smaller ones are ideal for compact desks.  
  • Extras Matter: RGB lighting, water resistance, and non-slip bases are important for day-to-day use. These, however, must align with your workflow and not disrupt it. 

Final Takeaway 

If you spend hours at your desk and rely on your phone throughout the day, a wireless charging desk mat is a small investment with everyday benefits. Choose one that matches your desk size, charging needs, and usage style, and enjoy a smarter, more organized workspace.  

Whether you’re building a home office, upgrading a gaming setup, or simply want a cleaner desk, our list has the right wireless charging desk mat to make a noticeable difference in daily comfort and convenience.

title.rendered: Stanford’s Popular iOS Development Course Is Now Free for Spring 2025

content.rendered:
Those keen on mastering iOS development without the hefty price tag of a bootcamp have often turned to Stanford’s CS193p, a well-loved option on the web. It is now even easier to dive into.

Stanford University has refreshed its CS193p course, officially titled Developing Applications for iOS using SwiftUI, for Spring 2025. The updated release includes all 16 lecture videos available for free, along with comprehensive supporting materials.

What’s Available in This Update

Since 2020, Stanford has shared CS193p openly, moving away from iTunes U to more accessible platforms like YouTube and the university’s own course website. The full Spring 2025 series is now live, giving learners access to every one of the 16 lectures through the course website and a dedicated YouTube playlist.

What You Won’t See: IOS 26 And Xcode 26 Features

Before getting started, it is important to know that these lectures were recorded before the release of Apple’s iOS 26 and Xcode 26. Stanford notes that while the code used in the course is largely compatible, it does not reflect the latest platform changes.

As a result, the course does not include coverage of newer additions such as Xcode 26’s built-in LLM assistance or the Liquid Glass interface design introduced in iOS 26.

Why The Course Still Holds Value

Despite this limitation, CS193p continues to be highly recommended by experienced developers. As a Stanford-taught course, it focuses on building strong foundations in iOS development and presents the material in a clear, approachable way.

For beginners or developers looking to solidify their understanding of SwiftUI, the Spring 2025 release remains a structured, reliable, and completely free place to start.

acceptedAnswer.text: Apple’s official engraving service does not affect your AirPods warranty or AppleCare coverage. title.rendered: How to Download Your Instagram Data: Messages, Photos and Activity

content.rendered:
If you’ve been using Instagram for years, the platform knows far more about your activity than you might realize. Beyond the photos and Reels you post publicly, Instagram quietly stores private messages, search history, interaction patterns, account settings, and detailed activity logs tied to your profile. Over time, this information builds into a complete digital record of how you use the app.

So, if you are curious about what Instagram stores about your account or want a personal backup of your content, downloading your Instagram data is the only way to access it. Read on to find out how to download your Instagram data and what you’ll get.

Table of Contents
  • Why Download Your Instagram Data
  • What Does Instagram Data Download Include
  • How to Download Your Instagram Data
    • On the Mobile App
    • On the Web
  • Accessing and managing your downloaded Instagram data
  • Taking Control of Your Instagram Data…

Why Download Your Instagram Data

Downloading your Instagram data allows you to view the platform beyond the feed. It gives you access to the full record of your account, including content you posted years ago, private conversations, searches, and behind-the-scenes activity that is not visible in the app.

It also serves as a reliable backup. Accounts can be restricted, compromised, or removed without warning, and once that happens, recovering years of photos, videos, and messages becomes difficult or impossible.

For privacy-conscious users, the download offers clarity. It shows exactly what information Instagram retains about you, helping you better understand and manage your digital footprint.

Finally, if you plan to archive your content or move away from Instagram, downloading your data ensures you retain full control rather than leaving it locked within the platform.

What Does Instagram Data Download Include

When you request a copy of your Instagram data, the social media platform prepares an archive of all the information associated with your account. This includes:

  • All uploaded content, such as photos, videos, Stories, and Reels, along with captions and timestamps
  • Direct messages, comments, likes, saved posts, and account information, like profile details and settings
  • Followers and following data, including close friends, blocked accounts, pending follow requests, recent follow requests, recently unfollowed profiles, and removal suggestions.

Beyond visible content, the download also includes:

  • Your activity data, such as your search history, login information, device details, and interaction logs.
  • Metadata like location tags, upload dates, and engagement records.

Some advertising-related insights and inferred interests may be limited or summarized rather than fully detailed.

How to Download Your Instagram Data

The steps to download your Instagram Data are almost identical on both the mobile app and the web version.

On the Mobile App

  1. Open the Instagram app and head to your profile.
  2. Tap the hamburger icon in the top-right corner.
  3. Tap Accounts Center.
  4. Tap Your information and permissions.
  5. Now, tap Export your information.
  6. Next, tap the Create Export button.
  7. Select the profile you’d like to export information from.
  8. Choose whether to export the information to your device or to an external service.
  9. Here, you can:
    • Choose the information you want to export
    • Select a date range,
    • Choose your preferred file format
    • Select the email address for delivery
  10. Once done, tap the Start Export button.
  11. Enter your account’s password when asked.

On the Web

  1. Visit Instagram.com and sign in to your account.
  2. Click the More button in the sidebar.
  3. Select Settings from the pop-up menu.
  4. Click Accounts Center.
  5. Select the Your information and permissions option in the sidebar, then click Export your Information on the right.
  6. Click the Create Export button.
  7. Select your Instagram profile.
  8. Now, choose whether to export the information to your device or to an external service.
  9. Here, you can customize your export, select your notification email, and choose your preferred format.
  10. Once done, click the Start Export button.
  11. Enter your account’s password when asked

Accessing and managing your downloaded Instagram data

When your Instagram data export is ready, you’ll receive an email stating “Your Meta information download is ready.”

You can either click the link in the email or manually go to the Export Your Information page in Meta’s Accounts Center. Once there, you’ll find your Instagram data archive under Available downloads.

From the moment you receive the email, you’ll have four days to download the file. If you miss this window, the export expires, and you will need to submit a new request.

When you tap the Download button, Instagram will ask you to verify your identity by entering your account password. 

This extra step ensures that only the account owner can access and download the exported data. Once the password is confirmed, the download begins.

After the download completes, you can unzip the file in the Files app on your device and access the exported folders within.

If you choose to export your information directly to an external service or device, Instagram will notify you in two ways.

  • An email confirmation.
  • An in-app notification once the transfer is complete.
Note Instagram may take up to 30 days to prepare and send your export link, especially for accounts with large amounts of data

Taking Control of Your Instagram Data…

Downloading your Instagram data gives you full control over your content and insight into how your account has been used over time. It is also useful for backups if you’re preparing to leave the platform entirely. So, if you’ve ever wondered how much of your digital life lives inside Instagram, this post answers that question completely.

Have you ever downloaded your Instagram data, or are you planning to do it now? Share your experience or questions in the comments below.

FAQs

How often can I download my Instagram data?

There is no strict limit on how often you can request your data. However, frequent requests may take longer to process, especially for large accounts. In most cases, it is best to request a new export only when you actually need an updated copy of your information.

Is downloading Instagram data safe?

Yes. Downloading your Instagram data through the app or Accounts Center is a secure, password-protected process. Only you can request and access the export. That said, the downloaded file contains sensitive personal information, so it should be stored securely and not shared with third-party services or unknown apps.

  • Best Instagram filters and effects for stories and reels
  • How to hide your active status on Instagram

"The founder of iGeeksBlog, Dhvanesh, is an Apple aficionado, who cannot stand even a slight innuendo about Apple products. He dons the cap of editor-in-chief to make sure that articles match the quality standard before they are published."

About Dhvanesh

Ever since teenage years, gadgets and technology have held a special place in Dhvanesh's heart. This fascination with gadgets and their inner workings fueled a lifelong passion for exploration and troubleshooting. Disassembled electronic items scattered around the house became a familiar sight during his younger years, a testament to this insatiable curiosity.

From SEO Expert to Apple Evangelist

After completing his IT engineering diploma, Dhvanesh's professional journey began with a 4.5-year stint as an SEO executive, honing valuable digital marketing skills. However, the desire to share tech knowledge and connect with a like-minded community proved stronger. In 2012, Dhvanesh embarked on a new adventure, founding iGeeksBlog. This blog became a haven for Apple enthusiasts and tech aficionados seeking insightful and in-depth information about everything Apple.

A Decade of iGeeksBlog: Leading the Apple Charge

In the past 12 years, Dhvanesh has donned multiple hats at iGeeksBlog. As the founder, he has steered the blog’s vision, ensuring it remains a trusted resource for Apple users worldwide. Additionally, he has been serving as the CEO of iGeeks Media Private Limited for the past 4 years, overseeing the company's growth and development.

Beyond Writing: A Multifaceted Approach

Dhvanesh isn't just a prolific writer, having penned hundreds of articles for iGeeksBlog. He has also served as the blog’s Editor-in-Chief and Content Strategist, ensuring a consistent flow of high-quality content that caters to the diverse needs of the Apple user base. The passion for exploration extends beyond the written word. He has created numerous YouTube videos for iGeeksBlog, providing visual demonstrations and engaging directly with the audience.

Staying Connected with the Apple Ecosystem

Dhvanesh's dedication to the Apple community goes a step further. Currently, he also manages the iGeeksBlog+ weekly newsletter, delivering curated Apple news, gadgets, apps, tips and tricks straight to subscribers' inboxes. This unwavering commitment to Apple technology and a genuine desire to empower fellow users make him a valuable asset to the iGeeksBlog team.

title.rendered: ChatGPT Voice Feature Will Be Removed From Mac App

content.rendered:
If speaking to ChatGPT on your Mac has become second nature, brace yourself for an upcoming change that might disrupt your routine. OpenAI has announced that the Voice feature in the ChatGPT macOS desktop app will be discontinued on January 15, 2026. After this date, using Voice through the Mac app will no longer be an option.

For those who rely on Voice for daily interactions with ChatGPT, this small update note carries significant consequences.

Table of Contents
  • The Announcement Appeared Discreetly In A Mac App Update
  • What Changes On January 15, 2026
  • Where ChatGPT Voice Will Continue To Work
  • Why OpenAI Is Removing Voice From The Mac App
  • What Mac Users Should Do Now

The Announcement Appeared Discreetly In A Mac App Update

OpenAI included a clear message in the release notes for the ChatGPT Mac app, stating:

  • Voice on the macOS desktop app will be phased out, effective January 15, 2026.
  • OpenAI’s reason for this change is to focus on “more unified and improved voice experiences” across its applications.
  • No other functionalities of ChatGPT on macOS will be affected.

To clarify, this is not about shutting down the entire Mac app or altering ChatGPT as a whole. It is specifically the end of the Voice feature in the native macOS app.

What Changes On January 15, 2026

It is crucial to understand that this is not an abrupt shutdown. It is a planned phase-out.

Once that date arrives:

  • Voice will no longer function within the ChatGPT Mac app.
  • Users relying on the Mac app for spoken interactions will need to move to another supported platform.

OpenAI also stresses that this change does not signal the decline of the Mac app itself. Other macOS features will remain untouched, meaning text-based chats and the core app experience will continue as usual.

Where ChatGPT Voice Will Continue To Work

Although Voice is leaving the Mac app, OpenAI confirms the feature is staying active elsewhere. Voice will continue to be available on:

  • Chatgpt.com through a web browser
  • iOS
  • Android
  • The Windows app

If you prefer speaking instead of typing, or enjoy conversational voice responses, you can still do that. You will just need to use one of these supported platforms instead of the macOS desktop app.

Why OpenAI Is Removing Voice From The Mac App

OpenAI says the decision is driven by a desire for consistency. The company wants to build more unified and improved voice experiences across all its apps.

While OpenAI has not shared technical details or confirmed whether Voice could return to the Mac app in the future, the wording suggests this is more of a restructuring than a rejection of voice interaction. Voice features work best when they feel familiar and reliable across devices, and that level of consistency often requires changes behind the scenes.

Also read: New ChatGPT for Mac Update Adds Game-Changing Record Mode and Cloud Drive Access

What Mac Users Should Do Now

If Voice plays a role in how you use ChatGPT on a Mac, some preparation can help avoid frustration later:

  • Mark January 15, 2026, as the cutoff date for Voice in the Mac app.
  • Try using Voice on chatgpt.com ahead of time so the transition feels natural.
  • If you use Voice across devices, make sure you are comfortable with it on iOS or Android, where support will continue.

While removing a single feature from one app may sound minor, it can feel disruptive when it affects established habits. Still, OpenAI is keeping Voice available in several other places and frames this move as part of a broader effort to improve the overall voice experience rather than eliminate it.
